State controller ledgers
Public licensing & entity APIs

Cross-match entity/kinship/lien records and filter by minimum net fee threshold
Route verified dossiers into compliant outreach and claim execution

Docket-to-contact latency (hours)
Net recovery / conversion rate

Unclaimed property & judgment dockets
Surplus auction manifests

Lock in contingent recovery agreements or below-intrinsic buyouts

Claim approval rate
Days from filing to disbursement

positioning_alternatives.title: The Commercial Judgment Recovery Desk
positioning_alternatives.subtitle: Build a four-person recovery pod around enforceable judgments, documented authority, lawful asset research, and counsel-led execution.
positioning_alternatives.audience: Commercial recovery operators serving business creditors with entered money judgments and sufficient records to establish enforcement authority.
positioning_alternatives.research_basis: Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 69 generally ties federal judgment execution to state procedure unless a federal statute applies. California Code of Civil Procedure section 683.020 illustrates why judgment age and applicable renewal rules belong in initial screening. A docket entry alone does not establish collectability.

positioning_alternatives.title: Priority Before Pursuit
positioning_alternatives.subtitle: Choose commercial enforcement files by reachable equity, competing claims, bankruptcy status, and the cost of the next lawful step.
positioning_alternatives.audience: Attorney-supported recovery teams handling commercial judgments against businesses or guarantors with identifiable assets.
positioning_alternatives.research_basis: 11 U.S.C. section 362 establishes the automatic stay framework; 11 U.S.C. section 522 addresses bankruptcy exemptions. UCC section 9-317 supplies a model priority rule involving security interests and lien creditors, subject to its exceptions and state enactment. These authorities support asset-specific screening rather than equating judgment principal with realizable cash.

positioning_alternatives.title: The Recovery Fee Ledger
positioning_alternatives.subtitle: Turn collected judgment payments into traceable creditor remittances, earned service fees, and reconciled operator economics.
positioning_alternatives.audience: Small recovery firms and creditor-service teams that need reliable payment allocation, deadline ownership, and commercial-file classification.
positioning_alternatives.research_basis: 15 U.S.C. section 1692a defines covered debt by its primarily personal, family, or household purpose; commercial labeling alone is insufficient. 12 CFR section 1006.38 supplies validation requirements where Regulation F applies. 15 U.S.C. section 1681b limits consumer-report access to permissible purposes. These rules support documented classification and controlled research, while fee recognition follows the actual service agreement and applicable accounting treatment.

chapters.question_prompt: What exactly is judgment recovery, how is real operator revenue recognized vs underlying asset/client GMV, and what separates durable small-team moats from fragile beginner hype?
chapters.title: What Exactly Is Judgment Recovery?
chapters.subtitle: Commercial Docket Intelligence, Attorney-Led Execution, Assignment Authority, Bankruptcy Stays, and Lien-Priority Economics
chapters.executive_summary: Judgment recovery converts an existing court award into collected money through verified authority, asset intelligence, priority analysis, and lawful enforcement. Candidate #8 ranks #28 with a 79/100 Money-to-Manpower Score: a high-leverage operator play when case selection beats case volume. This chapter maps 15 operating plays, separating commercial collection workflows from counsel-led privacy-claim evaluation. Recognized service fees, not judgment balances or client recoveries, support the scorecard: Conservative revenue of $60,000 produces $12,000 annual owner profit; Base revenue of $280,000 produces $84,000; Scaled revenue of $500,000 produces $200,000. Durable advantages come from reliable docket evidence, enforceable authority, disciplined spending, and reconciled client funds. An insolvent debtor, superior lien, or bankruptcy stay can defeat an otherwise impressive award.

key_metrics.label: Conservative
key_metrics.context: Annual recognized service fees; excludes client collections and judgment face value
key_metrics.note: 20% net margin; $12,000 annual owner net profit; 1 FT + 3 C

key_metrics.label: Base
key_metrics.context: Annual recognized service fees; excludes client collections and judgment face value
key_metrics.note: 30.0% net margin; $84,000 annual owner net profit; 1 FT + 3 C

key_metrics.context: Annual recognized service fees; excludes client collections and judgment face value
key_metrics.note: 40% net margin; $200,000 annual owner net profit; 2 FT + 4 C (6 people)

sections.heading: 1. Define the mandate before valuing the judgment
paragraphs: Judgment recovery is the business of helping a judgment creditor turn an existing court award into money through permitted investigation, negotiated payment, and authorized enforcement. The judgment establishes an obligation; it does not establish liquidity, lien priority, or an executable asset. A commercial supplier holding a $150,000 award against an empty corporation may recover nothing, while a smaller award against an operating business with reachable receivables may justify immediate attention. Start with the entered judgment, docket, party identities, service history, payment history, and any appeal, stay, satisfaction, or assignment. Then distinguish the named debtor from similarly named entities and from owners who are not personally liable. A corporate judgment does not automatically reach a member's house or an affiliate's bank account. The operator sells disciplined recovery work, not the assertion that every award has cash behind it. The client retains the underlying economic claim unless a valid transaction transfers it. Counsel handles legal judgments and appearances where required; sheriffs, marshals, and other authorized officials execute process under applicable procedure. An operator's practical contribution is organizing reliable evidence, controlling case spending, maintaining deadlines, and ensuring that each dollar received reaches the correct ledger and beneficiary.

Choose one contractual role before accepting documents or quoting fees. A research provider delivers factual records under a fixed scope. A collection agency pursues payment under the licenses, bonds, communications rules, and client-fund requirements applicable to its locations and activities. An assignee for collection needs a valid assignment and a jurisdiction-specific determination of who may enforce or appear. Assignment does not erase unauthorized-practice restrictions or guarantee that a business entity can represent itself. A counsel-support operator supplies records and administration without selling legal representation or taking an impermissible share of legal fees. An outright purchaser buys an economic asset and bears acquisition risk; that model requires accounting distinct from this volume's service-fee scorecard. Commercial debt also demands classification rather than a label supplied by a salesperson. Under 15 U.S.C. § 1692a(5), the federal consumer-debt definition turns on the underlying transaction's personal, family, or household purpose. State collection laws can cover additional conduct or obligations. Record the original transaction, debtor type, geography, proposed contact methods, and operator role in an intake memorandum. If those facts change, reassess the operating requirements before treating the matter as another routine commercial file.

The defensible starting niche is commercial post-judgment work with documentary authority and identifiable execution routes, not a warehouse of stale awards. Screen the obligation's age, renewal history, debtor operations, asset location, creditor priority, expected expenses, and likely collection timing. PACER and official state portals can establish procedural events; county recorder systems and secretary-of-state records add ownership and lien clues. None independently proves that an asset is available to satisfy this creditor. A recorded mortgage, perfected security interest, statutory lien, exemption, or co-owner can materially change the result. For example, an illustrative $100,000 asset with $80,000 senior claims and $15,000 sale costs leaves only $5,000 before other deductions, not a six-figure opportunity. Use a written spend ceiling and a documented stopping condition for every file. A $900 investigation cannot be justified by multiplying judgment face value by an optimistic success rate without considering realizable proceeds and fee entitlement. The five archetypes below are different operating businesses, not interchangeable branding choices. Select the one whose authority, capital demands, and evidence workflow match the team, then refer unsuitable files rather than quietly changing roles after a promising asset appears.

sections.heading: 2. Map fifteen plays to evidence, unit economics, and fallback routes
paragraphs: The fifteen-row matrix maps two supplied play identifiers and thirteen chapter-local operating workflows; it does not imply fifteen separate statutory collection powers. The first supplied play, public_record_api_intelligence, turns fragmented county dockets, probate registries, unclaimed property ledgers, and public APIs into reviewable leads. For an illustrative batch, 1,200 records at $0.20 processing cost require $240; six analyst hours at $50 add $300. If four files survive identity, authority, age, and asset screening, the $540 batch costs $135 per qualified file before outreach or enforcement. That number measures research efficiency, not revenue or expected recovery. Preserve the source URL, retrieval time, case identifier, extraction version, and human review result. A probate entry may identify an estate proceeding without proving the judgment reaches estate property; an unclaimed-property entry may concern a different person or require a specialized claimant process. Respect portal terms, access controls, and published request limits. When APIs disappear or access becomes unreliable, switch to scheduled bulk FOIA/public-record exports where applicable, official data feeds, and low-frequency cached queues. Federal FOIA does not govern state court access; identify the actual custodian and governing state or local records procedure instead.

The second supplied play, cipa_vppa_wiretap_pixel_settlement_arbitrage, is adjacent counsel-led claim evaluation, not an automatic source of enforceable judgments. Support genuine tracking-related privacy matters using authorized evidence collection, preserved disclosure and permission records, and factual technical analysis. Counsel must evaluate standing, statutory applicability, parties, limitations, injury, defenses, and available remedies before any demand. California Penal Code §§ 631 and 637.2 and 18 U.S.C. § 2710 have distinct elements; the presence of a network request does not establish a violation. Preserve browser version, timestamps, relevant page text, user interaction history, and a minimally necessary HAR export, protecting credentials and unrelated personal information. An illustrative eight-hour authorized evidence packet at $125 per hour yields a $1,000 support invoice, not ownership of claimed statutory damages. Accept only compensation arrangements permitted for the operator's actual role, and do not manufacture incidents or multiply demands from unreviewed scanner output. If evidence or standing fails, close the unsupported matter and offer authorized privacy-remediation audits instead. Only a resulting enforceable judgment enters the post-judgment workflow described here. Keep this adjacent service's contracts, records, and economics separate from a commercial creditor's existing award and from the canonical recovery scenarios.

For the remaining workflows, select the enforcement route from the asset and procedural facts rather than from a preferred sales pitch. Trade-credit files can reward entity resolution and repeat-creditor relationships. Equipment cases require serial numbers, ownership evidence, and a senior-security-interest review. Real-property cases require recording analysis, title work, exemptions, and realistic sale costs. A receivable is useful only if the account debtor owes collectible money and the jurisdiction permits the proposed process. Federal enforcement generally follows state procedure under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 69, subject to applicable federal statutes; a federal docket is not a universal shortcut around local execution requirements. Build a repeatable packet containing authority, asset evidence, priority analysis, estimated costs, and counsel's selected procedure. The illustrative fees below are pricing mechanisms for different services, not additive components of the canonical forecast. Quote each scope separately and prohibit double billing the same activity. Every row also names a failure trigger because a durable niche must survive adverse facts. A useful fallback may be monitoring, a narrower factual report, negotiated payments, referral, or closure. It is never unauthorized access, pressure against unliable relatives, or execution after a known stay.

callout.title: Buy better evidence before buying more case volume
callout.body: Veteran operators preserve the chain from source record to collectible proceeds and stop spending when that chain breaks.
items: Store the original judgment and every assignment beside the current docket; a searchable lead list cannot establish enforcement authority.
Date-stamp asset and lien checks, then refresh material facts before expensive process rather than reusing an old equity estimate.
Negotiate staged research scopes with explicit dollar ceilings so an insolvent debtor does not consume the entire case budget.
Keep a source-health register for each county portal, including permitted access methods and the official export fallback.

sections.heading: 3. Recognize earned fees and reconcile the three profit cases
paragraphs: The scorecard's revenue boundary is recognized service fees, not client asset value. Maintain separate figures for judgment face amount, remaining enforceable balance, gross collections received, client liabilities, reimbursable case costs, earned operator fees, and operating expenses. A $100,000 judgment that produces a $20,000 collection under an illustrative 25% recovery-fee agreement creates $5,000 of operator fees, not $100,000 or $20,000 of revenue. Before separately agreed expenses, the other $15,000 belongs to the creditor. Recognize fees under the actual contract and applicable accounting policy when performance and entitlement support recognition; a contingent claim, pending appeal, disputed distribution, or reversible payment requires specific analysis rather than an automatic cash-equals-revenue rule. A refundable advance is not earned merely because it reaches the bank. Likewise, a settlement signed today does not justify booking the entire face amount of future installments. Have the accountant document treatment of contingencies, refunds, recoverability, and principal-versus-agent presentation. Route legal fees, filing charges, and creditor distributions to their proper owners and accounts. Fees legally awarded to counsel do not automatically become operator revenue, and a receipt labeled recovery can contain several different economic components.

Reconcile the canonical annual cases without changing their staffing or margins. Conservative recognizes $60,000 of service revenue, incurs $48,000 of total expenses, and leaves $12,000 annual owner net profit at 20%, using 1 FT + 3 C. Base recognizes $280,000, incurs $196,000, and leaves $84,000 at 30.0%, also using 1 FT + 3 C. Scaled recognizes $500,000, incurs $300,000, and leaves $200,000 at 40%, using 2 FT + 4 C, or six people. One illustrative collection bridge is $300,000 collected at 20% for Conservative, $1,000,000 at 28% for Base, and $2,000,000 at 25% for Scaled. Those rates are explanatory assumptions, not additional canonical inputs or promised market prices. Different contract mixes can produce the same recognized revenue. Contractor headcount does not imply three or four full-time equivalents; measure actual hours and matter-level commitments. Keep staffing, contractor charges, acquisition costs, software, insurance, and unreimbursed enforcement spending inside the expense envelope. Report owner labor compensation consistently with the adopted scorecard convention instead of silently moving it between expense and profit. The scale case requires improved selection and throughput; hiring one additional employee alone does not explain the margin increase.

Capital timing is a separate operating problem from annual profitability. The supplied startup range is $10,000–$75,000, recurring monthly opex is $2,000–$12,000, and time to first deal is 6–24 months. Do not treat those ranges as a single fully funded package. Even six months at $2,000 consumes $12,000 before startup purchases or case advances; twenty-four months at $12,000 consumes $288,000. Narrow scope, retain outside income, secure appropriately structured funding, or reduce fixed commitments when the runway arithmetic does not work. The annual scenario expense totals include more than recurring overhead, so they must not be forced into the monthly opex range. Track each matter's unreimbursed cash exposure separately from accounting margin. An illustrative case producing $4,000 of earned fees with $1,200 of unreimbursed process costs and $800 of contractor work contributes $2,000 before shared overhead. A subsequent $1,000 fee refund reduces that contribution to $1,000 and requires a corrected ledger. Maintain a case-level reserve policy for disputed funds, payment returns, and potential disgorgement. Client balances cannot finance payroll, and an apparent collection win is not available working capital until ownership and distribution rights are resolved.

sections.heading: 4. Build a small-team moat around authority, priority, and cash controls
paragraphs: The highest-value control is knowing when enforcement must stop. Under 11 U.S.C. § 362, a bankruptcy filing can stay enforcement against the debtor or estate property; exceptions and relief require actual legal analysis. Check PACER before material collection steps and escalate filing notices immediately rather than waiting for the weekly portfolio review. Bankruptcy can also create recovery or return exposure for transfers under provisions such as 11 U.S.C. § 547; counsel should assess timing, parties, and defenses before the operator treats proceeds as irreversible. Exemptions require similarly specific analysis. Federal limits under 15 U.S.C. § 1673 can restrict garnishment of an individual's disposable earnings, while state law may provide greater protection. A commercial origin does not erase exemptions applicable to the property or person pursued. Real-property judgment liens depend on the relevant recording and attachment rules, including California Code of Civil Procedure § 697.310 where applicable. For personal property, UCC priority analysis can determine whether a lien creditor is subordinate to a secured party. Obtain a dated priority worksheet and an estimated net-realization range before spending on execution. Publicly visible ownership without reachable equity is a research result, not a collection plan.

Lawful data access is part of the production system, not a purchase-order footnote. Use public court records, authorized client documents, properly obtained discovery, and vendors whose access conditions fit the matter. LexisNexis Accurint or TransUnion TLOxp access, where available, carries contractual and use restrictions; a subscription does not authorize every search or downstream disclosure. For consumer reports, document an applicable permissible purpose under 15 U.S.C. § 1681b rather than assuming that holding any judgment grants unrestricted access. Avoid pretexting, credential sharing, and access to another person's private accounts. Store only evidence needed for the mandate, restrict exports, log access, and define retention and deletion schedules. Automate court deadline tracking and payment reconciliation, the two canonical leverage points, while keeping independent review for calculated dates, identity matches, interest adjustments, and satisfaction filings. A calendar should retain the triggering event, jurisdiction, rule source, reviewer, and reminder history; a payment workflow should retain bank evidence, allocation logic, and exception resolution. An incorrectly automated renewal date or misallocated creditor payment scales damage faster than manual work. Measure exception age and correction rate alongside throughput so automation earns trust through observed accuracy.

A small team becomes durable when it repeatedly rejects attractive-looking but uncollectible files and closes the loop on accepted ones. Give the owner responsibility for intake economics, client authority, and expenditure decisions; assign factual research, process coordination, and bookkeeping according to documented competence and permitted roles. Counsel remains responsible for legal strategy and required representation, with written scope and direct escalation paths. Review a weekly queue showing next action, cash at risk, days since source verification, bankruptcy status, expected net proceeds, and unreconciled balances. Measure qualified-file acceptance, fee yield per research dollar, collection cycle length, unreimbursed cost per resolved matter, and client-fund reconciliation breaks. Do not substitute judgment face value added to the pipeline for an economic performance measure. Build repeat business through accurate status reports that distinguish observed facts, counsel decisions, and estimates. When a matter closes, verify final allocations, resolve remaining costs, and coordinate the required satisfaction or release with the responsible party. Feed the outcome back into screening criteria without exposing one client's records to another. The resulting moat is a documented judgment about which cases deserve attention, supported by reliable operations, rather than a secret database or aggressive collection script.

chapters.question_prompt: Who writes the check in judgment recovery, what acute financial or statutory pain forces them to pay, and how do funds clear cleanly without circumvention or non-payment?
chapters.title: Who Pays, Why They Pay & How the Payment Rail Works
chapters.subtitle: Creditor Mandates, Debtor Liquidity, Attorney Trust Ledgers, Lien Priority, ACH Returns & Bankruptcy Claim Transfers
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #8, Judgment Recovery, ranks #28 with a 79/100 Money-to-Manpower Score across 15 mapped plays. The creditor buys execution discipline; the debtor supplies recoveries when lawful enforcement, settlement economics, or a transaction requiring lien release makes payment rational. Those are different counterparties, budgets, and accounting events. Build around documented authority, collectible assets, counsel-controlled enforcement, and a payment waterfall that separates client money from earned service fees. Canonical annual owner profits are $12,000 Conservative, $84,000 Base, and $200,000 Scaled, on recognized service-fee revenue rather than judgment face value. This chapter connects payer psychology to eight payment rails, fee protection, counterparty screening, distressed_asset_recovery, and chapter11_trade_claim_convenience_class_rollup, including explicit cost limits and fallback decisions.

sections.heading: 1. Identify the creditor buyer, debtor payer, and actual release authority
paragraphs: Begin every file with three separate identities: the creditor purchasing recovery services, the judgment debtor whose property may fund payment, and the person authorized to settle or release the judgment. A controller may approve a contingency engagement while only general counsel can approve a discounted satisfaction. A debtor's bookkeeper can transmit a wire without authority to bind the company to settlement terms. Obtain the entered judgment, current creditor identity, assignment chain, accrued balance calculation, and written settlement delegation before quoting outcomes. The creditor's acute pain is usually a written-off receivable, an aging reserve, or repeated spending on searches that never become enforceable remedies. The debtor's pain is different: a lawful levy, documented lien interfering with a sale, or the expense of continuing a dispute. None creates cash where assets are exempt, encumbered, or absent. Ask the creditor which employee owns the recovery budget, which person can approve enforcement expenses, and which signature releases collateral. Record those answers in Clio or an equivalent matter system with supporting documents, not merely a contact list. A signed engagement from someone without delegated authority is an operational defect, even when the underlying judgment is valid. Resolve that defect before ordering an expensive asset investigation.

Sell a bounded decision process rather than the nominal judgment balance. A creditor holding a $200,000 judgment might rationally authorize a $2,000 investigation when an identified receivable could support a $40,000 settlement. At an illustrative 25% service fee, that recovery produces $10,000 of operator revenue and $30,000 of creditor proceeds before separately agreed expenses. If the creditor also reimburses $2,000 from those proceeds, their economic recovery becomes $28,000; the reimbursement requires separate accounting rather than automatic treatment as additional margin. Compare this result with a documented alternative, such as another year of monitoring at a fixed cost, instead of claiming the full face amount is collectible. For debtor negotiations, establish a lawful reason to act now: an actual closing date, an enforceable order, or a documented discount expiration. Do not manufacture deadlines, threaten unavailable remedies, or imply criminal consequences for ordinary nonpayment. Counsel determines which execution procedures fit the forum. Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 69 generally points federal money-judgment enforcement toward state procedure unless a federal statute applies. The operating product is therefore a jurisdiction-specific collection plan backed by evidence, not a national script promising identical leverage against every debtor.

Counterparty screening must reach both sides of the engagement. Verify the creditor's existence through the relevant secretary of state, confirm the signer's authority, and resolve competing assignments before accepting instructions. Verify the debtor's exact legal identity, bankruptcy status, appeal posture, enforceability period, and ownership of the proposed payment source. PACER supports federal docket review; state court portals, county recording offices, and authorized UCC searches answer different questions and should not be treated as interchangeable asset databases. A UCC filing indicates a claimed security interest, not necessarily the current payoff or perfected priority against every asset. Obtain the relevant instruments and have counsel assess competing rights. Record whether the obligation arose from business activity or a consumer transaction; a judgment does not automatically remove consumer-debt protections. The FDCPA definition in 15 U.S.C. § 1692a concerns qualifying consumer obligations, while state collection laws may reach additional conduct or commercial claims. License coverage, lawful data access, and local representation rules belong in intake. A commercial focus does not authorize a nonlawyer to appear for another creditor or bypass restrictions through a paper assignment. When authority, identity, or coverage remains unresolved, restrict work to permitted screening and suspend enforcement spending.

callout.body: A collectible-looking asset is not enough. The file must identify who owns the claim, who may act, what may be reached, and who may receive the resulting funds.

sections.heading: 2. Select a settlement rail that preserves ownership and clearing evidence
paragraphs: Treat payment instructions as an executable settlement schedule, not an email containing bank coordinates. Identify the payer, beneficiary, receiving institution, matter reference, permitted amount, due date, allocation rule, and conditions for releasing the judgment. Prefer a lawfully designated attorney trust account or appropriately authorized escrow arrangement when disputed ownership, multiple beneficiaries, or conditional releases require controlled disbursement. The account must belong to the actual authorized custodian; calling an ordinary operating account escrow changes nothing. Verify wiring instructions through a previously established telephone number and document the callback. Reject instructions that redirect funds to an unrelated personal account, substitute cryptocurrency without an agreed operational reason, or change beneficiary details immediately before settlement. A genuine closing deadline is not a reason to skip identity controls. Wire transfers provide useful bank references but can still involve fraud, recall requests, legal restraint, or erroneous beneficiary information. ACH entries add authorization and return exposure whose timing depends on transaction type and applicable rules. No single hold period makes every payment final. Use the receiving bank's actual settlement evidence and counsel-approved release conditions; do not file a satisfaction merely because a debtor supplies a screenshot marked sent or a payment processor displays a provisional balance.

The eight rails below solve different problems and should not be sold as interchangeable checkout options. A retainer funds authorized work; it does not prove the debtor has paid the judgment. A statutory disbursement routes funds through a sheriff, court officer, or bankruptcy administrator under governing procedure. Factoring transfers economic rights or finances receivables and therefore changes counterparty risk rather than simply accelerating the same collection. Milestone holds are a contractual control layered onto an account and payment method, not an independent banking network. Platform checkout can simplify small installments, but Stripe or another provider must expressly support the actual collection activity and account structure. Processor reserves, chargebacks, and acceptable-use restrictions can defeat apparently convenient economics. Do not disguise recovery services as ordinary retail sales to obtain processing. Compare an illustrative $20,000 settlement paid by wire with the same settlement paid through a hypothetical card channel charging 3%: processing alone consumes $600 before disputes or reserves. That rate is a comparison assumption, not a vendor quote. The agreement must specify who bears permitted payment costs and whether they reduce the fee base. Adding an unauthorized collection charge to the debtor's balance can create a separate violation rather than protect margin.

Build clearing around a matter-level ledger with separate columns for gross receipts, lawful interest allocation, reimbursable costs, earned operator fees, counsel charges, creditor proceeds, and unresolved holds. Where a statute prescribes allocation, that rule governs before internal preferences; California Code of Civil Procedure § 695.221 provides one jurisdiction-specific allocation rule for money received in satisfaction of a money judgment. For an illustrative $40,000 recovery with a contractually permitted 25% operator fee and no separate deductions, record $40,000 received, $10,000 earned service revenue, and $30,000 payable to the creditor. The $30,000 never becomes operator revenue merely because it passed through a controlled account. If $2,000 of authorized creditor expenses are also reimbursed from proceeds, creditor cash falls to $28,000 under that expressly agreed waterfall. Whether the reimbursement is presented gross or net in business accounts requires a consistent accounting assessment. Reconcile bank activity, custodian statements, and individual client ledgers before disbursement; QuickBooks may support operating accounts but does not replace required trust-account controls. Use a second reviewer for beneficiary changes and outgoing distributions. After release conditions are satisfied, complete the jurisdiction's satisfaction procedure promptly. In California, § 724.010 addresses satisfaction of judgment; do not retain a satisfied lien as informal leverage for an unrelated fee dispute.

sections.heading: 3. Protect earned fees without confusing custody, legal fees, or revenue
paragraphs: Fee protection starts in the creditor engagement, not with secret control over debtor money. Define the covered judgment, recoveries included in the fee base, treatment of interest and costs, fee earning event, direct-payment reporting duty, termination mechanics, and any lawful, narrowly defined post-termination entitlement. Specify whether a fee arises on cleared cash, property actually received, or another measurable event; avoid billing on a settlement promise that may never perform. Require the creditor to notify the operator promptly when a debtor pays directly, and provide reasonable statement access to reconcile covered receipts. An enforceable payment direction acknowledged by the authorized custodian can reduce diversion, but it cannot override statutory priorities, trust duties, or another party's superior rights. Do not invent a lien merely by naming one in an invoice. Counsel should assess any assignment, security arrangement, or contractual remedy under the applicable law. Keep attorney compensation separate from the operator's lawful recovery-service compensation: a commercial agreement cannot authorize prohibited sharing of legal fees with nonlawyers. If the licensed and ethical structure cannot support the proposed contingent arrangement, redesign the permitted service scope and pricing rather than routing payments through an intermediary to conceal the same economics.

Reconcile the scorecard using service revenue only. For an illustrative portfolio with a uniform, legally permitted 25% service fee, the Conservative case requires $240,000 of annual client recoveries to produce $60,000 of recognized operator revenue. Deduct $48,000 of modeled operating expenses to obtain $12,000 annual owner net profit, a 20% margin, with 1 FT + 3 C. The Base case requires $1,120,000 of recoveries to produce $280,000 revenue; $196,000 of expenses leaves $84,000 profit at 30.0%, again with 1 FT + 3 C. The Scaled case requires $2,000,000 of recoveries to produce $500,000 revenue; $300,000 of expenses leaves $200,000 profit at 40%, with 2 FT + 4 C. These collection volumes explain the fee bridge, not additional scorecard revenue. The fee assumption must be replaced wherever statutory caps or negotiated terms differ. Expense totals include the full modeled cost burden; contractor headcounts do not establish full-time compensation for every contractor. The stated $2,000–$12,000 monthly operating range is an initial planning reference, not a ceiling overriding the annual scenario arithmetic. Base and Scaled annual expenses require explicit capacity and variable-cost budgets beyond a simplistic twelve-month multiplication of that reference range.

Underwrite each enforcement increment before committing portfolio capacity. Suppose a documented $50,000 reachable asset has a 40% probability of producing a full recovery after priority review, and the operator would earn 25% on collected cash. Expected service revenue is $5,000: $50,000 multiplied by 40% multiplied by 25%. If incremental operator-borne investigation and enforcement costs are $3,000, expected contribution is $2,000 before overhead, delay, and adverse outcomes. That estimate supports a bounded experiment, not an assertion that the $50,000 belongs in revenue. If a senior lien leaves only $10,000 reachable, the same calculation yields $1,000 expected fees and a $2,000 expected loss against those costs. Stop or obtain a genuinely different cost allocation instead of chasing sunk expenses. Require written authorization for third-party charges and clarify whether the creditor reimburses them even if recovery fails. Maintain separate aging for unpaid service invoices and uncollected debtor obligations; they have different counterparties and remedies. With $10,000–$75,000 startup capital and a stated 6–24 months to first deal, liquidity discipline matters as much as nominal margin. Reserve enough cash for already authorized work, and never borrow another client's proceeds to bridge a slow-paying matter.

callout.title: Make diversion difficult without taking unauthorized control
callout.body: Veteran operators protect fees with evidence, delegated authority, and reconciled receipts rather than aggressive language unsupported by the engagement or applicable law.
items: Attach a sample waterfall to the engagement using a $40,000 recovery; have the creditor confirm the fee base and every expense deduction.
Use one matter reference across settlement instructions, bank records, invoices, and satisfaction documents so direct payments remain traceable.
Obtain current senior lien payoff information before buying another asset search; the priority subtraction can eliminate the entire recovery thesis.
Recheck bankruptcy immediately before a levy, settlement demand, or distribution decision, and route any newly discovered filing to counsel.

sections.heading: 4. Price distressed recoveries and bankruptcy claims against verified distributions
paragraphs: For distressed_asset_recovery, the judgment-recovery variant is a dormant commercial judgment whose creditor lacks current asset intelligence or an economical enforcement partner. Suppose a $100,000 judgment supports a verified $30,000 settlement and a lawful 25% contingent service fee. Operator revenue is $7,500, creditor proceeds are $22,500 before separately agreed costs, and $1,500 of operator-borne incremental work leaves $6,000 contribution before overhead. The judgment's face amount is neither revenue nor a collectible asset estimate. Screen title to the claim, renewal requirements, debtor ownership, exemptions, senior liens, and likely enforcement expense before treating the opportunity as mispriced. Other variants include tax-sale overages, unclaimed state funds, and government surplus assets, but their ownership rules, solicitation restrictions, fee caps, and acquisition mechanics differ. Do not import the illustrative 25% rate into a statutory recovery program without checking its requirements. An asset acquisition spread also belongs in a separate investment model rather than the canonical service-fee scorecard. The specified fallback is diversification across multi-state dockets and attorney-backed filing partnerships where required. Diversification must preserve state-specific licensing and procedure; it does not mean mass filing against unverified debtors. Stop an uneconomic file before using another jurisdiction merely to repeat the same unsupported asset assumption.

For chapter11_trade_claim_convenience_class_rollup, the economic payer is the estate or plan disbursing entity, not an operator pressuring the debtor outside bankruptcy. Review Schedule E/F, the claims register, proof of claim, underlying invoices, defenses, plan, disclosure statement, and distribution notices together. A scheduled trade balance is a lead, not proof that an undisputed allowed claim will receive the advertised convenience-class percentage. Consider a documented $10,000 claim with a supported 20% expected general-unsecured distribution. Purchasing it for $1,200 and spending $200 on diligence and transfer produces an illustrative $600 expected spread before overhead and time value: $2,000 expected proceeds less $1,400 committed cash. A downside distribution of 5% returns $500 and loses $900 against that same cash commitment. These proprietary purchase economics are separate from recognized recovery-service fees. Federal Rule of Bankruptcy Procedure 3001(e) governs relevant claim-transfer procedures, with different treatment depending on transfer timing and purpose. Check plan-specific aggregation, claim-splitting, election, and related-holder provisions before assuming that several purchased claims retain separate convenience-class benefits. If that thesis fails, stop affected purchases, enforce documented seller recourse where available, and price only supported general-unsecured recoveries. Seller recourse has value only when enforceable against a seller capable of paying.

Bankruptcy changes the operating path immediately. Under 11 U.S.C. § 362, the automatic stay generally restricts covered collection activity against the debtor and estate property, subject to statutory exceptions and court orders. A public docket alert should pause affected workflows for counsel review, not trigger a faster demand before competitors react. Section 502 addresses claim allowance, § 507 establishes specified priorities, and § 1122 governs classification subject to its terms; none establishes a universal convenience-class payout. Model the actual plan waterfall and timing. Outside bankruptcy, refresh credit evidence around meaningful events: a business sale, missed installment, new secured borrowing, returned payment, or proposed release. Separate observable facts from estimates in the matter record. A bank receipt proves a payment event; it does not prove future installment capacity. A property record identifies recorded interests; it does not establish realizable net equity. Automate docket deadlines and payment reconciliation, but require human review when ownership, priority, or authority changes. Close the loop with a monthly cohort report showing recovered cash, earned fees, unreimbursed expenses, collection duration, and stopped files. That report reveals whether the enterprise is earning the canonical margins or simply accumulating large judgments and contingent expectations that never clear into distributable money.

chapters.pull_quote: A judgment names an obligation; verified authority, reachable equity, and reconciled cash determine whether the operator earns anything.

statutory_citations.relevance: Federal money-judgment execution generally follows the procedure of the state where the court is located unless an applicable federal statute governs; also addresses discovery in aid of execution.

statutory_citations.relevance: Defines covered debt and debt collectors; distinguish qualifying consumer obligations from the chapter's commercial-debt focus.

statutory_citations.title: 15 U.S.C. § 1692f — Unfair practices
statutory_citations.relevance: For covered collection activity, subsection (1) restricts collection of amounts unless expressly authorized by the agreement creating the debt or permitted by law.

statutory_citations.title: 11 U.S.C. § 362 — Automatic stay
statutory_citations.relevance: Requires immediate assessment of stay restrictions before covered collection, enforcement, or property-control activity continues after a bankruptcy filing.

statutory_citations.title: 11 U.S.C. § 502 — Allowance of claims or interests
statutory_citations.relevance: Supports claim diligence focused on objections, allowance, and disallowance rather than treating every scheduled balance as an assured distribution entitlement.

statutory_citations.title: 11 U.S.C. § 507 — Priorities
statutory_citations.relevance: Identifies statutory priority categories relevant to modeling the distribution available to purchased trade claims.

statutory_citations.title: 11 U.S.C. § 1122 — Classification of claims or interests
statutory_citations.relevance: Addresses classification and permits a separate class of qualifying small unsecured claims for administrative convenience subject to its requirements; does not promise a particular payout.

statutory_citations.title: Federal Rule of Bankruptcy Procedure 3001(e) — Transferred claims
statutory_citations.relevance: Sets claim-transfer procedures that vary with timing and transfer type; incorporate required evidence, notice, and objection handling into acquired-claim operations.

statutory_citations.title: California Code of Civil Procedure § 695.221 — Allocation of receipts
statutory_citations.relevance: Provides a state-specific allocation rule for money received in satisfaction of a money judgment; apply the governing statutory allocation before discretionary internal ledger preferences.

statutory_citations.title: California Code of Civil Procedure § 724.010 — Satisfaction of judgment
statutory_citations.relevance: Addresses satisfaction through payment or creditor acceptance of a lesser sum and the associated acknowledgment requirement, subject to the statute's terms.

chapters.question_prompt: What are the real unit economics, gross-to-net margin deductions, scrub/reversal reserves, and working-capital float requirements for judgment recovery?
chapters.title: Unit Economics, Margin Waterfall & Working-Capital Float
chapters.subtitle: Recognized Recovery Fees, Rule 69 Enforcement Costs, Bankruptcy Holds, Contractor Waterfalls & Restricted-Cash Discipline
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #8, Judgment Recovery, ranks #28 with a 79/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. Across the volume's 15 mapped plays, the economic denominator is recognized service fees, never judgment face value or client recoveries. The canonical Conservative, Base, and Scaled cases produce $12,000, $84,000, and $200,000 annual owner net profit on $60,000, $280,000, and $500,000 revenue. This chapter converts those totals into paying-case yields, contractor costs, acquisition expense, enforcement disbursements, reversal allowances, and cash-conversion gaps. It also separates commercial judgment enforcement from settlement-claim administration and time-barred receivable resolution. The operating discipline is simple: price the collectible, legally reachable outcome; fund the waiting period; and keep client money outside the operating runway.

sections.heading: 1. Build the cohort ledger before valuing the judgment inventory
paragraphs: Start with one annual intake cohort and keep four denominators separate: screened matters, accepted engagements, paying resolutions, and recognized operator fees. The illustrative Conservative cohort accepts 60 engagements and produces 20 paying resolutions; Base accepts 200 and produces 80; Scaled accepts 300 and produces 125. Their respective paying-case rates are 33.33%, 40%, and 41.67%. Average client recoveries of $11,000, $14,000, and $16,000 generate $220,000, $1,120,000, and $2,000,000 of underlying recoveries. Applying illustrative contracted commissions of 30%, 27.5%, and 27.5% produces $66,000, $308,000, and $550,000 of provisional fee calculations. These are settlement-workpaper amounts, not an instruction to invoice before an enforceable fee entitlement exists. Scrubs and reversals reduce those calculations to the canonical $60,000, $280,000, and $500,000 recognized revenue. Net recognized fees per paying resolution therefore equal $3,000, $3,500, and $4,000. A larger judgment balance does not improve that yield unless reachable assets, priority, exemptions, and collection timing improve with it. Store the original judgment, accrued-interest calculation, renewal date, assignment chain, and client distribution separately so neither principal nor pass-through recoveries accidentally enter the operator's sales account. Use distinct matter identifiers for affiliated debtors rather than merging their assets into one apparently collectible balance.

The waterfall below is an illustrative allocation that reconciles exactly to the supplied scorecard; it is not a claim that the scorecard specifies each expense account. Gross fee reductions equal $6,000, $28,000, and $50,000, or 9.09% of provisional fees in every scenario. Split those amounts evenly between eligibility or entitlement scrubs and expected fee reversals. A scrub removes a duplicate engagement, unsupported assignment, excessive commission calculation, or otherwise unearned fee before recognition. A reversal allowance addresses an already estimated fee exposed to repayment, disputed allocation, or collection failure. Apply the accounting treatment appropriate to the actual contract and facts; an invoice alone does not establish earned revenue. Contractor delivery labor covers investigator, document, and permitted outsourced casework charges, not an assumed share of an attorney's legal fees. Attorney engagement terms and professional fee-sharing restrictions must be resolved separately. Enforcement expense covers operator-borne disbursements only. If a client reimburses an advance, classify that transaction according to the principal-agent relationship and contract rather than adding both the reimbursement and the original client recovery to service revenue. Retain a document link supporting every deduction so cohort yield can be reconstructed after staff changes.

Acquisition spending is $9,000, $28,000, and $40,000 across the three cases. Dividing by accepted engagements gives intake CAC of $150, $140, and $133.33; dividing by paying resolutions gives outcome CAC of $450, $350, and $320. Report both because an apparently inexpensive lead channel can deliver insolvent debtors and consume enforcement capital without producing fees. Total recognized operating deductions are $48,000, $196,000, and $300,000, leaving the required owner profits. The administrative and employee-support line includes budgeted nonowner payroll, payroll burden, insurance, and administration; contractor charges remain separate. The owner supplies the first full-time role in this illustration, with residual profit serving as owner compensation before personal tax. The Scaled second full-time role is funded within its $44,000 support allowance, an assumption requiring local compensation validation before hiring. Contractor counts indicate available specialists, not four full-time salaries. This distinction explains how headcount and a lean cost base coexist without pretending labor is free. Maintain a separate replacement-cost view for the owner's work, but do not silently deduct that imputed wage from the canonical profit figures. Display owner hours beside profit whenever comparing this operation with a business requiring less personal case management.

callout.title: Price reachable cash, not impressive docket balances
callout.body: Experienced recovery operators protect fee yield before spending on enforcement.
items: Compare accepted-case CAC with paying-case CAC monthly; stop the referral source whose low intake price conceals repeated insolvency.
Obtain a dated lien-priority workpaper before commissioning expensive asset work; senior secured debt can consume the entire reachable balance.
Quote a separate operator-borne disbursement ceiling in the engagement and obtain written instructions before exceeding that ceiling.
Tag each lost fee by entitlement defect, debtor insolvency, bankruptcy interruption, or allocation dispute so reserve changes address actual loss mechanisms.

sections.heading: 2. Turn reversal exposure and enforcement decisions into priced controls
paragraphs: Reserve architecture needs three separate accounts rather than one undifferentiated haircut. First, the pre-recognition scrub removes fee calculations that fail entitlement testing. Second, expected commission reversals reduce recognized fee estimates where appropriate. Third, an expense provision covers losses on operator-funded advances or other distinct obligations. The same failed matter must not generate both a full fee reversal and another expense for that identical lost fee. Record each exposure with matter identifier, exposure type, maximum amount, probability assumption, expected settlement date, and supporting document. Review cohorts by origination quarter and jurisdiction, because a single blended percentage can conceal concentrated assignment defects or an enforcement practice that stopped working. The model's expense provisions are $4,000, $14,000, and $20,000, separate from fee reductions. They are accounting estimates, not automatically funded bank balances. When a provision becomes an actual cash payment, update the cash forecast without charging the same expense twice. If cash losses recur steadily, include expected payments in the recurring cash-cost baseline rather than permanently treating the provision as noncash. Keep release authority with someone other than the caseworker whose production metric improves when reserves fall; reserve releases should follow evidence, not a monthly revenue target.

For each enforcement step, calculate incremental expected contribution using only value still available after superior claims and applicable exemptions. An illustrative $40,000 reachable commercial recovery at a 30% commission creates $12,000 of potential fees. A 35% collection probability produces $4,200 expected gross fees. A 10% fee-loss allowance reduces that to $3,780; subtract $1,200 of incremental contractor work and $900 of operator-borne enforcement expense to obtain $1,680 expected contribution before shared overhead and funding cost. If new lien evidence cuts collection probability to 15%, expected fees after the allowance fall to $1,620 and contribution becomes negative $480. The correct response is to pause that step, renegotiate who funds it, or pursue a cheaper lawful route. Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 69 generally directs federal money-judgment execution through the procedure of the forum state unless a federal statute applies. It does not make every asset attachable or authorize an unlicensed operator to practice law. Counsel should select writs, discovery, and local process after reviewing ownership, priority, exemptions, service requirements, and the available evidence. Record why the selected remedy beats the next cheapest lawful alternative.

A bankruptcy filing can destroy the timing assumptions without immediately resolving the ultimate claim value. Under 11 U.S.C. § 362, the automatic stay generally restricts collection and enforcement against the debtor and estate property, subject to statutory scope and exceptions. Stop affected activity promptly, route the matter to counsel, and move expected receipts out of near-term available cash until a supported collection path exists. Do not infer permission to continue from an old writ, a judgment assignment, or a creditor's instruction. Separately, distinguish legal collectibility from economic collectibility: a valid judgment against an insolvent entity may have almost no realizable value. Before approving an advance, retain a current docket check, asset-ownership evidence, priority analysis, and a written recovery budget. PACER can support federal docket review, while state court portals and official UCC filing offices supply different pieces of the record; none alone proves net reachable assets. Lawful data access must be documented for every investigative source. A consumer report requires a permissible purpose under 15 U.S.C. § 1681b, and availability through a vendor does not itself establish that purpose. Recheck material facts before disbursing additional enforcement money, not merely at original intake.

callout.title: Four checks before committing the next enforcement dollar
callout.body: The next disbursement requires a supported entitlement, remedy, budget, and cash source.
items: Verify the judgment, assignment chain, renewal status, and applicable licensing requirements for the operator's actual role and jurisdiction.
Check bankruptcy status, exemptions, and senior claims before treating a discovered asset as reachable recovery.

Confirm that unrestricted operator cash funds the step and that client distributions remain fully reconciled and segregated as required.

sections.heading: 3. Fund the DSO and payout-lock gap without borrowing client money
paragraphs: Define DSO here as days from supported fee recognition to collection of the corresponding cash, then define payout lock as additional days before collected operator fees become unrestricted and transferable. These are sequential intervals in this illustration; if a processor's reported settlement interval already includes its hold, do not add the same days again. Conservative assumes 60 days of DSO plus 15 locked days, Base 75 plus 30, and Scaled 90 plus 45. Exclude the initially noncash expense provisions from annual operating deductions to obtain $44,000, $182,000, and $280,000 of cash-cost proxies. Divide by 365 and multiply by the combined delay. The resulting steady-state float requirements are approximately $9,041, $52,356, and $103,562. Add separately identified liquidity buffers of $10,000, $15,000, and $25,000 to obtain planning targets of $19,041, $67,356, and $128,562. Those buffers cover timing dispersion and emerging cash losses; they are not additional expenses in the profit waterfall. This simplified calculation assumes reasonably even cash spending and receipts. It is a screening calculation rather than a substitute for a weekly forecast when recoveries arrive in a few large settlements or disbursements precede recognition by several litigation cycles.

The supplied startup capital range of $10,000–$75,000 does not automatically fund a mature Scaled operation. Its illustrative $128,562 liquidity target requires retained earnings, documented financing, client-funded disbursements where permitted, or slower intake. Do not make that gap disappear by presenting client collections as working capital. Equally, the stated $2,000–$12,000 monthly operating range should not be mistaken for a ceiling on every variable delivery and enforcement payment at scale. This chapter treats it as an early operating-envelope assumption; Scaled cash costs average about $23,333 monthly before irregular loss payments. The 6–24 month time to first deal introduces another funding layer because the steady-state DSO calculation starts only after fee recognition. At a deliberately lean $2,000 monthly pre-revenue burn, six months requires $12,000 and twenty-four months requires $48,000 before setup costs or a larger enforcement campaign. At $12,000 monthly, the corresponding burn becomes $72,000–$288,000. Build a dated ramp forecast rather than adding every maximum mechanically: some startup expenditure overlaps the later operating cycle, while other advances occur much earlier. Restrict commitments when the forecast minimum cash balance breaches the chosen buffer, even if the annual income statement still shows attractive profit.

Use a thirteen-week cash forecast with separate columns for client funds, restricted operator fees, unrestricted operator cash, contractor payables, enforcement commitments, and probable refunds. Reconcile the matter subledger to bank activity and the general ledger weekly. QuickBooks Online or Xero can hold the operating ledger, while an appropriately configured trust-account system should handle funds subject to trust rules; software selection does not determine the legal classification. Import payment references into the matter record, match partial receipts against approved distributions, and prevent automatic transfers when allocation remains disputed. Court deadline tracking should generate a named owner's task and escalation date rather than merely an email reminder. Payment reconciliation should flag unmatched deposits, duplicate fees, stale checks, and changes to beneficiary instructions. Require independent verification of changed bank details through a previously established contact channel. Financing costs are absent from the canonical waterfall unless absorbed within existing expense allowances. For example, a continuously drawn $50,000 facility at 12% annual interest costs $6,000 before fees and would reduce Base owner profit from $84,000 to $78,000 if incremental. Show that adjustment explicitly instead of preserving the headline margin by hiding funding expense inside client distributions or unreconciled clearing accounts.

sop_steps.title: Close the matter-level fee worksheet
sop_steps.action: Match each recovery to entitlement evidence and approved distributions.
sop_steps.detail: Separate client principal, operator fees, reimbursable advances, scrubs, and reversal estimates before posting revenue.

sop_steps.title: Schedule unrestricted availability
sop_steps.action: Assign expected collection dates and additional release dates.
sop_steps.detail: Record DSO and payout locks as nonoverlapping intervals; exclude stayed, disputed, and client-owned amounts from available operating cash.

sop_steps.title: Rebuild the thirteen-week funding forecast
sop_steps.action: Load contractor invoices, enforcement commitments, payroll, and probable refunds.
sop_steps.detail: Compare the lowest weekly unrestricted balance with the liquidity buffer and defer unfunded commitments before ordering work.

sop_steps.action: Tie bank balances, matter subledgers, and general-ledger accounts.
sop_steps.detail: Investigate unmatched receipts, stale disbursements, reserve releases, and changed payment instructions before releasing operator distributions.

sections.heading: 4. Stress the canonical cases and ring-fence adjacent recovery plays
paragraphs: Stress revenue, delivery cost, and timing independently before combining them. With operating deductions held fixed, a 10% reduction in recognized fees lowers Conservative owner profit to $6,000, Base to $56,000, and Scaled to $150,000. A separate 25% contractor cost increase lowers profits to $7,500, $66,500, and $172,500. Applying both shocks produces $1,500, $38,500, and $122,500. These are sensitivity outputs, not replacements for the canonical scorecard. Break-even recognized fee yield, holding total deductions and paying-case counts constant, is $2,400 per paying case in Conservative, $2,450 in Base, and $2,400 in Scaled. Compare those thresholds with the modeled $3,000, $3,500, and $4,000 yields. If slower cases also require additional attorney work, the fixed-cost assumption understates damage; enter that expense separately. A thirty-day cash delay alone does not reduce accrual profit, but it increases funding requirements by approximately $3,616, $14,959, and $23,014. Any borrowing interest then reduces profit. Set intake limits from the combined downside forecast rather than from the best single margin percentage. A business can remain profitable on paper while failing to fund the contractor invoices necessary to collect the next recovery.

For b2b_class_action_contingency_recovery, track court-approved commercial settlement funds involving payment-card interchange, freight, auto parts, commercial insurance, and SaaS through official notices and administrator instructions. Some funds can be multibillion-dollar programs, but fund size is not operator revenue or an individual claimant's entitlement. Treat the supplied 85–90% small-business nonfiling assertion as an unverified sourcing hypothesis until program-specific evidence supports it. An illustrative ten verified businesses receiving $10,000 each generate $100,000 client payouts. A permitted 25% contingency produces $25,000 provisional fees; a 20% payout or entitlement haircut leaves $20,000 recognized fees. Subtract $7,000 contractor labor, $2,000 acquisition, $3,000 document and administration expense, and $2,000 distinct operating-loss provision to leave $6,000 contribution before shared overhead. At a permitted 33% fee with otherwise identical assumptions, contribution becomes $12,400. These examples remain outside the canonical totals unless explicitly allocated into their existing revenue and cost budgets. Verify operating-business identity and primary processor or vendor statements; follow court-approved third-party claim-filing riders where applicable. If a program prohibits the arrangement, do not substitute an informal authorization. Suppress unsupported claims and use only an administrator-permitted service structure with documented claimant authority and the actual filing deadline.

For out_of_statute_zombie_debt_portfolio_settlement, distinguish limitation periods, extinguishment rules, credit-reporting periods, and any separate judgment-enforcement period before buying or contacting accounts. This consumer-sensitive adjacency does not inherit the commercial judgment workflow. An illustrative $500,000 face-value portfolio bought for $5,000 is purchased principal, not $500,000 revenue. If lawful voluntary resolutions yield $20,000, subtract the $5,000 purchase outlay, $6,000 servicing expense, and $3,000 remediation cash allowance to obtain $6,000 cash contribution before shared overhead; accounting revenue recognition requires a separate purchased-receivable policy. Under a distinct service-only arrangement, $20,000 client collections at 25% produce just $5,000 operator fees, yielding negative $4,000 contribution against those same servicing and remediation amounts. Do not merge these two ownership models. Regulation F, 12 CFR § 1006.26(b), prohibits covered debt collectors from suing or threatening suit on time-barred debt. State law may impose additional restrictions or extinguish obligations. Credit reporting under 15 U.S.C. § 1681c follows separate limits; payment does not authorize re-aging delinquency information or promising deletion of accurate records. Exclude extinguished or otherwise uncollectible obligations. Suppress affected accounts, correct reporting, and suspend collection until counsel approves remediation; never fund the core recovery operation with assumed proceeds from legally defective inventory.

chapters.question_prompt: How do you allocate startup capital ($10,000–$75,000 USD) and configure a lean, low-opex ($2,000–$12,000 USD/mo) production stack without wasting cash on bloated overhead?
chapters.title: Startup Capital, Lean Infrastructure & Pre-Flight Stack
chapters.subtitle: Reserve-First Budgets, PACER Screening, Segregated Recovery Accounts, Arizona ABS Boundaries & UCC Priority Controls
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #8, Judgment Recovery, ranks #28 with a 79/100 Money-to-Manpower Score across a portfolio of 15 mapped plays. Its capital advantage comes from screening enforceable commercial judgments before funding enforcement, not from buying an oversized software stack. Allocate 60% of startup cash to working-capital reserves, separate client proceeds from earned fees, and release investigation dollars against documented recovery hypotheses. The canonical annual owner-profit cases are $12,000 Conservative, $84,000 Base, and $200,000 Scaled; revenue means recognized service fees, never judgment principal. This chapter specifies twelve infrastructure layers, reconciles fixed overhead with total scenario expenses, and tests pre-launch authority, bankruptcy screening, payment controls, and lawful adjacent-play economics before the first creditor mandate.

sections.heading: 1. Reserve 60% of Capital Before Buying Investigations or Infrastructure
paragraphs: Build the business around a reserve account, not an office lease. The allocation below assigns 60% of each $10,000, $30,000, or $75,000 capitalization to unrestricted working capital, leaving 40% for launch commitments. Keep client money entirely outside this calculation: creditor proceeds cannot finance subscriptions, payroll, or another creditor's investigation. Treat the legal allocation as money for collection-license analysis, engagement terms, assignment review, local enforcement counsel, and entity formation; it is not a prepaid litigation campaign. Purchase business-owned equipment with disk encryption and supported operating systems rather than leasing furnished space. Release the investigation allowance by file: an illustrative $100 identity-and-docket screen followed by a separately authorized $250 asset-hypothesis review limits initial exposure to $350. Ten such files consume $3,500 before writs, process service, or contested hearings. That workload exceeds the smallest launch investigation bucket, so the $10,000 operator must screen fewer files or negotiate properly documented creditor-funded costs. Establish who bears an unsuccessful search before ordering it. A judgment's face amount does not replenish reserves, and a recorded lien does not create spendable cash. Fund evidence that can change a collection decision, then stop when the evidence shows no reachable equity.

Match the reserve to the collection clock before accepting the business model. At illustrative fixed monthly burns of $2,000, $5,000, and $12,000, the corresponding $6,000, $18,000, and $45,000 reserves provide only 3.0, 3.6, and 3.75 months of coverage. The stated six-to-twenty-four-month time to first deal therefore creates a real funding gap; first collection can arrive later still. Six months of fixed overhead requires $12,000, $30,000, or $72,000, producing reserve shortfalls of $6,000, $12,000, or $27,000 before variable enforcement spending. At twenty-four months, those shortfalls become $42,000, $102,000, and $243,000. Do not disguise that gap with projected settlements. Launch part-time with funded overhead, obtain a committed capital source, reduce the workload, or defer launch. A revolving facility counts only when executed, drawable, and compatible with its covenants; an expected approval is not liquidity. Keep a weekly thirteen-week cash forecast and a monthly twenty-four-month survival model. Include contractor retainers, deductible exposure, license renewals, and creditor reimbursement timing. Set a cash floor covering the next ninety days of committed overhead plus authorized case commitments; below that floor, stop discretionary investigations rather than borrowing from remittances.

Set entity, banking, and insurance boundaries before the first engagement. Obtain an EIN, confirm required state registrations, and determine whether the activities require a collection-agency license, bond, registered manager, or attorney involvement. An assignment is not permission for a nonlawyer to represent another party or an entity in court. Use an operating account, a reserve account, and the legally required client-funds arrangement; where counsel receives recoveries, their applicable trust-account rules control. Document signers, beneficial owners, payment permissions, and bank-service restrictions on collection businesses. Ask the broker to confirm coverage for the actual activity under errors and omissions, cyber, and crime policies, including contractor acts, social-engineering loss, defense costs, and exclusions. A certificate alone does not establish coverage. The bookkeeper should maintain a separate creditor liability ledger, case-cost ledger, and earned-fee ledger. For an illustrative $10,000 receipt with a contractual 25% earned fee and no reimbursable costs, $7,500 remains payable to the creditor and $2,500 is operator revenue once recognition conditions are satisfied. Reconcile the receipt, bank settlement, agreement, and remittance before moving the fee. Resolve disputed allocations through counsel rather than letting a spreadsheet silently decide ownership of funds.

callout.title: Buy the Next Decision, Not the Whole Investigation
callout.body: Experienced recovery operators spend in small evidence-producing increments and protect the cash needed to finish viable files.
items: Ask enforcement counsel for a written stop-loss budget separating searches, service, writ issuance, contested hearings, and creditor-funded expenses.
Reuse a previously purchased docket document only after matching the case and checking whether later orders changed enforceability.
Request policy wording for collection activities and client-funds theft before paying the insurance premium; retain the broker's written explanation.

sections.heading: 2. Install Twelve Lean Layers Without Automating Legal Judgment
paragraphs: Use the twelve-layer matrix as a procurement worksheet, not a shopping list. Its dollar amounts are explicit United States planning assumptions for named tiers, not verified current offers; confirm checkout pricing, annual commitments, taxes, and eligibility before purchase. Select free tiers until a measured limitation affects controlled production. The illustrative paid core is one Google Workspace Business Starter seat at $7 monthly equivalent, one Bitwarden Teams seat at $4, one Backblaze Computer Backup license at $9 monthly, and one Microsoft Defender for Business seat at $3 monthly equivalent: $23 per month before tax, usage, or additional devices. The low software subtotal does not replace the $2,000 minimum modeled overhead; counsel availability, insurance, bookkeeping, communications, and administration still cost money. Annual-billed products can require upfront cash even when the worksheet displays monthly equivalents. Give contractors named, limited accounts only when their assignments require access, and revoke those accounts when work ends. Never share the owner's mailbox or password-vault login to avoid another seat. Track each subscription's owner, renewal date, export format, cancellation procedure, and purpose. Upgrade only after recording the hours or errors the purchase will eliminate.

Build a lawful evidence pipeline before connecting a data vendor. PACER supplies federal docket material, while state courts and county recorders remain essential for state judgments and liens. CourtListener RECAP can reduce duplicate document purchases, but a cached document does not prove current docket status. A UCC search identifies filings and indexed parties; it does not prove the balance, validity, or priority of every asserted obligation. Commercial database access through providers such as LexisNexis Risk Solutions or Thomson Reuters CLEAR requires appropriate contracting, credentialing, and a documented lawful use. Obtain a written quote rather than inventing a per-search price. Under 15 U.S.C. § 1681b, access to a consumer report requires a permissible purpose; possessing a commercial judgment does not automatically authorize a report about every officer, relative, or guarantor. Restrict the initial case register to case identifiers, parties, counsel, deadline sources, authorized costs, and payment status. Store sensitive documents in restricted folders rather than embedding them in broad task boards. Require source URLs, retrieval dates, entity-match evidence, and an analyst conclusion for each purchased finding. Delete redundant exports under the retention schedule while preserving records subject to legal holds.

Automate deadline tracking and payment reconciliation as exception-reporting systems, not autonomous enforcement engines. Create separate fields for judgment entry, renewal eligibility, renewal deadline, service events, recorded liens, bankruptcy checks, and controlling jurisdiction. Each calculated deadline needs a source rule, calculation explanation, responsible person, and independent review by qualified counsel where required. A generic ten-year timer can be wrong for the jurisdiction, judgment type, or procedural history. Send internal reminders at ninety, sixty, and thirty days, but require the operator to acknowledge the underlying docket check. For payments, match bank transaction identifiers to a unique case identifier and agreement version; segregate partial payments, reversals, processor charges, and disputed creditor allocations. Do not let a successful webhook establish that funds are irrevocable or distributable. Test duplicate notifications, failed bank debits, delayed settlements, and a changed remittance account. Use a callback to a previously verified creditor contact before changing payment instructions. At one hundred monthly receipts, saving six minutes per match releases ten hours; at a $35 internal hourly cost, the illustrative gross benefit is $350 before software and exception handling. Buy automation only when measured savings exceed its cost and its failure path is documented.
