sections.heading: 2. Turn registry hits into an evidence-preserving enrichment waterfall
paragraphs: Implement the waterfall with PostgreSQL for structured case data, encrypted object storage for documents, and a scheduler such as systemd timers or a managed job runner. A small desk does not need a distributed crawler to handle hundreds of active judgments. Separate matters, parties, identifiers, assets, instruments, observations, deadlines, and cash events into different records. Give every observation a source URL, source record key, retrieved_at timestamp, effective date when available, parser version, content hash, and access-purpose reference. Preserve raw files separately from extracted text. Hash the original bytes with SHA-256; hashing only normalized text loses the ability to identify an altered original. OCR with Tesseract can make scanned judgments searchable, but an operator must verify debtor names, amounts, dates, and decretal language against the image. Store money as integer cents and record currencies explicitly. Retain exact court identifiers including leading zeros and punctuation. Use stable source keys for idempotent ingestion so a repeated download creates a fresh observation without duplicating the instrument. A document correction should supersede an earlier interpretation, not erase the earlier record or its review history.

Resolve identity before buying broader enrichment. Begin with the judgment caption and entity number, then compare formation jurisdiction, historical names, service records, and business addresses. Match a business using identifiers and corroborating documents rather than name similarity alone. Keep individual guarantors separate from corporate defendants; an owner's relationship to a company does not automatically make their assets available for the company's debt. Route ambiguous matches into manual review and prohibit automated enforcement exports from that queue. The Fair Credit Reporting Act treats permissible purpose as a substantive condition, including collection-related access only where the statutory conditions apply; a commercial judgment does not itself authorize every consumer report. Likewise, motor vehicle personal information requires an applicable Driver's Privacy Protection Act exception, not merely a useful investigative purpose. Restrict Accurint or TLOxp access to contracted uses, individual accounts, and retained purpose records. Never pretext a bank, employer, or relative to obtain protected information. If a licensed report produces only an address association, return to original records or attorney-directed discovery. The correct fallback for an unresolved person match is a narrower research task, not a larger automated contact campaign.

Instrument the pipeline around false positives and missed events, not just successful HTTP responses. A login page returned with status 200 is not a valid docket response. Validate content type, expected record identifiers, pagination totals, and required fields before accepting an extract. Maintain redacted fixtures for a normal result, empty result, restricted response, amended filing, duplicate debtor name, and scanned document. Python unittest, sqlite3 scratch databases, and structured logging provide enough diagnostics for the first production version. Add exponential backoff with jitter, a bounded retry count, and a manual exception queue; authentication failures should stop that connector rather than trigger repeated login attempts. A weekly review should sample ten accepted matches and every rejected critical event, measuring incorrect joins and stale records. Track cost per verified lead, not cost per returned row. For example, fifty $4 reports cost $200; if only five produce verified new asset leads, acquisition cost is $40 per verified lead before labor. If ten review hours cost an assumed $35 each, the combined cost rises to $110 per verified lead. Stop the purchase tier when that evidence does not improve expected net recovery.

sections.heading: 3. Convert court events and payment evidence into controlled operator economics
paragraphs: Deadline tracking begins with jurisdiction-specific rules, not a universal judgment expiration formula. Store the triggering event, applicable authority, counting convention, review owner, and supporting document for each renewal, response, or enforcement task. Under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 69, execution generally follows the procedure of the state where the federal court sits unless a federal statute applies. That makes state-specific templates essential even inside one federal docket connector. California Code of Civil Procedure section 683.020 provides a useful example of a ten-year enforceability framework, but exceptions, renewal rules, stays, and the particular judgment still require review. A bankruptcy petition can trigger 11 U.S.C. section 362 before a search aggregator reflects it. Screen at intake, monitor active matters, and repeat the check immediately before consequential enforcement activity. Upon credible bankruptcy notice, pause affected collection tasks and obtain counsel's assessment of the debtor, property, claim, and any applicable order. Do not automatically resume after dismissal, discharge, or a vendor status change. The system should generate a review task with the underlying court event, preserving a visible record of who authorized the next step and why.

Payment reconciliation is the second high-value automation lever because cash errors destroy both margin and client trust. Import bank transactions through an authorized bank feed or controlled statement export, match receipts to matters, and hold ambiguous matches outside the disbursement queue. Record gross receipts, earned service fees, reimbursable expenses, client payable balances, and reversals separately. Do not calculate distributable money from a dashboard total that includes uncleared deposits. The illustrative $20,000 receipt with a 25% earned fee produces $5,000 of operator revenue, not $20,000, and does not justify recognizing the entire unpaid judgment. Apply the actual contract, accounting policy, and relevant custody requirements. If counsel holds client money, reconcile your matter ledger to counsel's remittance statement rather than assuming your own operating account should receive it. A daily exception report should flag duplicate payment identifiers, receipts without matters, fees exceeding agreed terms, stale checks, and transfers without supporting settlement instructions. Require a second person to verify changed payment destinations through a previously established contact channel. Keep bank credentials outside source-control files and limit each integration to the minimum access needed for its specific reconciliation function.

Reconcile the desk to the canonical scenarios before approving more subscriptions. Conservative recognizes $60,000 of annual service fees, incurs $48,000 of all-in costs, and leaves $12,000 owner net profit at 20% with 1 FT + 3 C. Base recognizes $280,000, incurs $196,000, and leaves $84,000 at 30.0% with 1 FT + 3 C. Scaled recognizes $500,000, incurs $300,000, and leaves $200,000 at 40% with 2 FT + 4 C. Contractors are staffing capacity, not an assumption that everyone works full time. The stated $2,000–$12,000 monthly operating range is not a cap on total scenario expenses; modeled all-in costs also need to absorb applicable labor, case costs, and other delivery expenses without double counting. At an illustrative $5,000 earned fee per completed matter, the revenue cases require 12, 56, and 100 fee-producing matters respectively. These are capacity equivalents, not predicted collections. A $300 research package on a $5,000 fee opportunity consumes 6% of the fee before enforcement expense and labor. If verified equity disappears or senior claims consume likely proceeds, stop incremental spending rather than trying to rescue sunk research costs with a more aggressive collection tactic.

sections.heading: 4. Separate tax-credit origination intelligence from credit ownership and recovery proceeds
paragraphs: The mapped play transferable_tax_credit_brokerage_syndication uses project intelligence to find potential sellers, but its data model must remain separate from judgment enforcement. Do not describe DOE or EPA as nationwide interconnection queue operators. DOE-funded Berkeley Lab queue research aggregates project information, while regional grid operators and utilities maintain their respective queues; EPA redevelopment datasets identify sites, not transferable tax credits. Use PJM downloads, Berkeley Lab's Queued Up research, EPA RE-Powering resources, state film-office publications, and state historic-preservation records as lead sources only. Confirm whether a project exists, who owns the eligible taxpayer entity, whether construction or production milestones were satisfied, and whether the relevant credit is actually transferable. A queue application, film listing, historic designation, or brownfield address proves none of those conclusions by itself. Public records may also omit private project ownership changes and current credit allocations. Obtain seller authorization and original eligibility documents before sending a buyer any transaction-specific representation. Keep recovery-client information out of origination outreach unless its use is independently authorized; a distressed developer's appearance in a judgment file does not make confidential client intelligence available for another business line.

IRC section 6418 permits specified eligible federal credits to move under its conditions; it does not create a freely resalable bearer instrument. The transferee cannot subsequently transfer the purchased credit under that provision. Therefore, the proposed buy-low, sell-high economics must be structured as a direct eligible seller-to-buyer transfer with a documented intermediary fee or other properly analyzed arrangement, not an operator taking title and flipping the same federal credit. For an illustrative $100,000 eligible credit, an $0.85 seller realization and $0.94 buyer outlay create a $9,000 gross economic spread. If documented transaction expenses are $4,000, the remaining contribution is $5,000 before overhead. These are illustrative negotiating assumptions, not current quotes, insurance prices, or additions to the canonical recovery scenarios. When the desk acts as agent, recognize its earned fee under the applicable accounting treatment, not the $100,000 credit face value or the buyer's entire wire. Counsel and the tax specialist must allocate seller consideration, buyer costs, escrow instructions, and intermediary compensation consistently with transfer rules. Georgia film, Louisiana film, historic rehabilitation, and brownfield programs require separate state-specific transferability analysis rather than borrowed federal assumptions.

The risk fallback is strict: never warehouse unhedged credits or advance the seller money against an uncommitted buyer. Require buyer-funded simultaneous escrow, a direct authorized transfer, and a binding tax-credit insurance policy meeting the transaction's required non-cancelable coverage terms. Do not represent that such coverage is always available or that it eliminates exclusions, recapture exposure, or claims disputes. If the insurer cannot provide the required terms, or the buyer will not fund the coordinated closing, decline the transaction rather than weaken this play's conditions. Verify insured parties, coverage period, exclusions, cancellation provisions, claims control, and the specific credit facts covered. Federal pre-filing registration is part of the applicable process, not proof that the IRS has approved substantive eligibility. State program certificates likewise need program-specific review. Keep an immutable closing packet with seller authority, eligibility workpapers, buyer commitments, escrow confirmations, insurance evidence, and fee invoices. Price origination research separately from recovery cases: twenty leads at an assumed $25 research cost consume $500 before specialist diligence. Continue only when documented buyer demand and eligible supply justify that spend, never because a public dataset makes distressed projects easy to enumerate.

chapters.title: Contracts, Statutory Guardrails, Licensing & Outreach Scripts
chapters.subtitle: FDCPA Classification, Bankruptcy Stays, State Collection Licenses, Assignment Economics, Lien Priority & Verified-Party Scripts
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #8, Judgment Recovery, ranks #28 with a 79/100 Money-to-Manpower Score across a volume containing 15 mapped plays. The operating edge is disciplined classification: commercial versus consumer obligations, ownership versus servicing, investigation versus legal representation, and recoverable assets versus senior liens. Build contracts around collected fees, documented authority, capped enforcement budgets, and accountable counsel. Conservative economics recognize $60,000 revenue and $12,000 annual owner profit; Base recognizes $280,000 and $84,000; Scaled recognizes $500,000 and $200,000. Client recoveries are never service revenue. This chapter supplies multi-state screening rules, contract controls, verified-party outreach, and a bounded litigation-finance extension that separates lawful funding from unauthorized fee sharing, mispriced medical records, and assumed settlement proceeds.

sections.heading: 1. Classify the obligation before selecting an enforcement rail
paragraphs: Start every file with the transaction that created the debt, not the caption on the judgment. Under 15 U.S.C. § 1692a(5), the federal consumer-debt definition turns on primarily personal, family, or household purposes; reducing an obligation to judgment does not erase its origin. An invoice owed by a manufacturer for production equipment ordinarily presents a different federal analysis from a personal medical bill. A natural-person guarantor does not automatically convert a business obligation into consumer debt, but mixed-use facts require review. Record the underlying agreement, purchase purpose, creditor identity, judgment debtor, judgment date, and present owner. Separately test whether the operator qualifies as a debt collector under § 1692a(6), including the principal-purpose branch; purchasing a claim does not automatically remove that exposure. Regulation F, 12 CFR part 1006, implements federal consumer collection requirements where applicable. State licensing and conduct rules can reach further than federal coverage, including commercial accounts. Build one classification memo per account and retain the supporting documents. If the origin cannot be established, suspend debtor outreach while obtaining the source contract; a commercial-looking company name is insufficient evidence.

Build a jurisdiction worksheet using the operator's location, debtor's location, judgment forum, asset situs, and proposed communication channels. Washington's RCW 19.16.110 requires collection-agency licensing subject to statutory definitions and exceptions; RCW 19.16.250 supplies operational restrictions. Florida separates commercial collection registration under Fla. Stat. § 559.543 from consumer collection registration under § 559.553. California's Financial Code § 100001 addresses licensing for debt collection as defined in that division; do not extend a consumer-focused definition mechanically to every commercial judgment. For each jurisdiction, retain the definition, exemption analysis, license number where required, bond or financial-security evidence, renewal date, and responsible supervisor. Counsel admission is a separate question from collection licensing. A collection credential does not authorize legal representation, and an assignment does not necessarily let a nonlawyer appear for an entity. California Business and Professions Code § 6125 illustrates the practice-of-law boundary. Local counsel should determine whether domestication, execution, discovery, and renewal require filings or appearances reserved to lawyers. In federal court, Rule 69 generally borrows state execution procedure, subject to applicable federal law. Assign the operator document assembly, docket monitoring, and reconciliation; assign legal strategy and court advocacy to authorized counsel.

Before spending on a levy, check enforceability, priority, exemptions, and bankruptcy separately. A favorable judgment is neither a first-priority lien nor proof of collectible equity. Obtain the entered judgment, service record when relevant, appeal and stay status, assignment chain, renewal history, and existing satisfactions. Search PACER Case Locator for bankruptcy indicators and verify likely matches against the actual docket. Section 362 of title 11 generally stays covered collection activity upon filing; exceptions and stay-relief orders require account-specific analysis. A discharge raises the separate injunction under § 524. Route potential matches to counsel immediately and freeze affected communications and enforcement spending pending resolution. Check secured financing statements, recorded liens, tax liens, and ownership interests before estimating available proceeds. UCC § 9-317, as enacted locally, addresses certain lien-creditor priority conflicts but does not replace the full priority analysis. Federal wage-garnishment limits in 15 U.S.C. § 1673 coexist with more protective state provisions and statutory exceptions. Personal exemptions can matter when enforcing against an individual commercial guarantor. Use a written waterfall: realizable sale proceeds minus senior claims, exempt amounts, sale expenses, and enforcement costs. Decline an apparently valuable asset when that waterfall produces no economic recovery.

sections.heading: 2. Contract for a defined service, a defensible fee, and a reconciled waterfall
paragraphs: Use separate instruments for creditor services, claim assignment, and attorney representation. The services agreement should identify the judgment and parties, define permitted research and administration, and reserve litigation decisions and representation to authorized counsel. An assignment must specify what interest transfers, when transfer occurs, who supplies original evidence, and who bears defects in ownership; a collection-only assignment is not the same economic instrument as an outright purchase. Require warranties concerning title, prior assignments, credits, settlements, pending insolvency proceedings, and authority to engage the operator. Attach the opening balance calculation and applicable interest method rather than describing the balance as whatever the docket shows. State who may approve settlements, release liens, accept installments, incur costs, and instruct counsel. Require written client authorization for defined expenditure thresholds and material settlement changes. A $1,500 investigator authorization must not silently become a $9,000 levy budget. Specify withdrawal rights when a client withholds evidence or requests prohibited conduct. Termination provisions should preserve lawful record retention, deadline transfer, accounting, and client property return. They should not permit the operator to withhold indispensable court records as leverage for a disputed invoice. Counsel's engagement remains independently governed by professional duties.

Define the fee trigger as an agreed percentage of eligible, actually collected cash, with explicit treatment of reversals, direct debtor payments, noncash settlements, interest, costs, and preexisting payment plans. Do not invoice a success fee merely because an asset search identifies a bank account. An illustrative 20% service fee on $1,400,000 annual eligible recoveries yields $280,000 recognized service revenue, matching the Base scorecard without treating creditor money as sales. Its 30.0% net margin leaves $84,000 owner profit and $196,000 total operating costs. At the same illustrative fee, $300,000 recoveries produce the Conservative $60,000 revenue, $48,000 costs, and $12,000 profit; $2,500,000 recoveries produce the Scaled $500,000 revenue, $300,000 costs, and $200,000 profit. These are reconciliation identities, not additional forecasts. Teams remain 1 FT + 3 C, 1 FT + 3 C, and 2 FT + 4 C respectively. The 20% illustration is neither an attorney-fee split nor a universal market rate. Establish custody arrangements allowed by the relevant jurisdiction, reconcile each receipt to the judgment ledger, and remit client funds under the governing agreement and applicable rules. Record cost reimbursements according to the actual accounting relationship rather than automatically inflating fee revenue.

Draft anti-circumvention around identified accounts and an objectively bounded tail period, not a permanent claim over every future creditor relationship. Require prompt notice of direct payments, credit for recoveries already reported, and a dispute process for attribution. Exclude unauthorized work and double recovery. A liability cap should identify the covered damages, measurement period, insurance interaction, and negotiated exclusions for fraud, intentional misconduct, misuse of client funds, or other liabilities that cannot validly be limited. Avoid a purported cap that contradicts mandatory statutory remedies. Specify governing law, forum, escalation timing, and any arbitration terms; the services contract does not alter the debtor's procedural rights or the enforcing court's jurisdiction. For data ownership, separate client records and account-specific work product from reusable operator templates, software, and methods. Third-party database licenses remain subject to vendor restrictions even when the client paid the search expense. Set export format, retention periods, access revocation, deletion exceptions, and incident notification duties. PACER documents, LexisNexis Accurint outputs, bank records obtained through lawful process, and consumer reports have different provenance and use restrictions. Maintain a source-and-purpose ledger instead of promising unrestricted ownership of every assembled data point. Require subcontractors to follow the same account restrictions and return evidence when their engagement ends.

callout.title: Protect the fee by improving the evidence trail
callout.body: Experienced recovery operators reduce disputes before spending on enforcement, rather than relying on aggressive collection language afterward.
items: Attach a signed opening-balance schedule showing principal, lawful interest, credits, and recoverable costs before discussing contingent fees.
Ask counsel for a priority waterfall before buying a costly asset report; senior liens can eliminate the entire recovery thesis.
Require creditor notice of direct payments and match those notices against the monthly debtor ledger before calculating any fee.
Use separate deadline fields for renewal, lien duration, domestication, and counsel review; a single judgment-expiration field conceals different legal events.

sections.heading: 3. Use verified-party scripts and purpose-limited data access
paragraphs: Separate creditor acquisition from debtor collection in the CRM, sender identity, suppression lists, and script library. A creditor discovery email can say: "We provide commercial judgment research, payment reconciliation, and coordination with authorized enforcement counsel. If you have an unpaid business judgment, may we discuss its age, current owner, prior collection efforts, and the jurisdictions involved? Please do not email account numbers or sensitive personal records. We can arrange a secure document exchange after confirming authority." This is a services introduction, not a claim that assets have already been found. Commercial email must satisfy applicable CAN-SPAM requirements, including truthful routing and subject information, required identification, a valid postal address, and a functioning opt-out honored within the statutory period. Do not treat business-to-business prospecting as categorically exempt. During discovery, ask: "Who can authorize this engagement, who currently owns the judgment, and has any attorney or agency retained rights to proceeds? Has the debtor filed bankruptcy, appealed, or disputed a payment credit?" Request documentary answers before quoting collectibility. A salesperson should never promise recovery, describe counsel as already retained, or suggest a court relationship that does not exist.

For a confirmed commercial obligation and a verified authorized recipient, use a narrow account discussion: "I am Jordan Lee with Harbor Recovery Services, acting for the judgment creditor under written authority. We are contacting you about case 24-CV-1182 in the named court. Are you authorized to discuss this business account? We can provide the judgment and a dated balance statement through a secure channel. If your records show payments, a stay, representation, or a dispute, please identify the relevant document so we can review it before discussing next steps." The names and case number here illustrate fields that must be replaced with verified facts. Do not use this commercial script as a substitute for required consumer disclosures. When the FDCPA applies, incorporate § 1692e(11) disclosures and provide the required validation information under § 1692g and 12 CFR § 1006.34, with applicable dispute handling. Respect represented-party and inconvenient-time restrictions. Avoid case details in messages that could reach third parties. Use a counsel-reviewed limited-content voicemail only when its regulatory conditions are met; adding a balance or demand can change its treatment. Log the recipient verification method without collecting unnecessary identity documents.

Configure communications as account-specific rules rather than a universal dialing cadence. Regulation F's telephone-frequency presumptions under 12 CFR § 1006.14 involve calls to a particular person about a particular debt and the period after a telephone conversation; they are not a license to make every technically counted call. Other harassment restrictions still apply. Review the TCPA, 47 U.S.C. § 227, and 47 CFR § 64.1200 before automated dialing, artificial or prerecorded voice calls, or campaign texts, considering the actual technology, recipient number, consent, revocation, and applicable exceptions. For investigations, query authorized public records first and retain source timestamps. A consumer report requires a permissible purpose under 15 U.S.C. § 1681b; the existence of a judgment is not a universal authorization to pull anyone's file. Confirm the relationship and purpose with counsel and the reporting provider. Driver records require a permitted use under 18 U.S.C. § 2721. Never obtain financial information through impersonation or false pretenses; 15 U.S.C. § 6821 directly addresses that conduct. Enforce role-based access, export logs, and vendor credentials assigned to individual users. If a source cannot document lawful access, discard the lead and use counsel-directed discovery instead.

sections.heading: 4. Bound the litigation-finance extension before committing docket capital
paragraphs: The mapped play litigation_finance_mass_tort_docket_securitization is a TRACK_1 extension, not ordinary post-judgment collection. Its proposed structure pairs an Arizona Alternative Business Structure or co-counsel firm with institutional litigation funding to assemble 1,000–25,000 retained plaintiffs across PFAS, AFFF, Paraquat, NEC, rideshare assault, and defective medical-device matters. These are proposed categories, not findings that any particular docket is viable. Arizona Supreme Court Rule 31.1 and ACJA § 7-209 govern the ABS framework; an Arizona license does not authorize nationwide nonlawyer legal practice or override another jurisdiction's professional rules. Co-counsel fee division must satisfy the applicable attorney-conduct requirements, and third-party funding must preserve counsel's independence and client-directed decisions. A nonlawyer recovery company cannot assume it may receive a percentage of legal fees merely by labeling itself a syndicate. Distinguish funding proceeds, firm ownership distributions within a permitted structure, lawyer-to-lawyer fee divisions, and ordinary contracted services. Counsel must also evaluate solicitation rules, privilege, conflicts, funding disclosure orders, and restrictions on assigning claims or proceeds. Retainers, medical evidence, and claimant relationships are not freely transferable inventory. Any proposed tranche transfer requires examination of client rights, contract assignability, confidentiality, and the receiving firm's authority.

The proposed $1,200–$2,500 acquisition cost per retained claimant means 1,000 claimants require $1.2 million–$2.5 million before additional record, expert, servicing, and funding expenses; 25,000 require $30 million–$62.5 million. Those capital requirements sit outside this volume's $10,000–$75,000 judgment-recovery startup range. At 1,000 claimants and $1,800 acquisition cost, a $1.8 million acquisition basis priced at the proposed 2.5x–4x multiple implies $4.5 million–$7.2 million gross transaction consideration. It does not establish an available buyer, realized gain, recognized service revenue, or collectible claim value. The proposed 35–40% settlement contingency must be tested against actual retainers, governing law, court orders, common-benefit assessments, and co-counsel arrangements. For illustration, 35% of a $10 million eligible settlement base is $3.5 million in gross contractual attorney fees before applicable allocations and expenses; it is not $3.5 million of recovery-operator income. Likewise, a proposed $6.50 HITECH patient-directed records request is not a universal procurement price. Under 45 CFR § 164.524(c)(4), qualifying individual access requests permit specified reasonable cost-based fees. HHS describes an optional $6.50 flat-fee method for qualifying electronic copies, while third-party requests and directives require separate analysis, including the Ciox decision's effect. Budget actual lawful request types, authorization handling, and custodian charges.

Use the proposed fallback as a set of underwriting questions, not a promise that diversification cures weak cases. Holding six to ten mass-tort or single-event commercial casualty categories can reduce concentration only when factual exposure, defendants, insurance, scientific evidence, and litigation outcomes are sufficiently independent. Correlation can reappear through shared funding markets or adverse evidentiary rulings. The proposal to pay media vendors only for EMR-verified retainers requires a prior professional-conduct review: paying per retained client can create prohibited recommendation or referral compensation even when records are authentic. Where that structure is impermissible, use lawful advertising arrangements with quality controls that do not purchase legal recommendations. Reject duplicate identities, unsupported exposure, unverifiable signatures, and records obtained beyond authorization. Offloading 50% of the illustrative $1.8 million cost basis means obtaining $900,000 of actual third-party capital or transfer proceeds, not booking a receivable against a hopeful buyer. Model recourse, repurchase duties, reserves, funder priority, and servicing costs before treating that cash as risk reduction. If transfer terms or ethics requirements fail, stop acquisition and retain only contractually supported servicing obligations. Keep this extension in a separately reviewed capital plan; the Conservative, Base, and Scaled judgment-recovery fee and profit figures remain unchanged.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #8, Judgment Recovery, ranks #28 with a 79/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. This chapter gives the volume's 15 mapped plays a shared automation architecture: authorized docket ingestion, evidence-linked LLM extraction, reviewed deadline calculations, payment reconciliation, and creditor referral loops. Target 70%+ less repetitive handling time without delegating enforcement decisions to software. The canonical annual owner profit cases remain $12,000 Conservative, $84,000 Base, and $200,000 Scaled, generated from recognized service fees rather than judgment balances or client collections. A four-person team owns exceptions, source verification, and attorney coordination; six people support the Scaled case. The design explicitly separates ordinary recovery fees from speculative lien acquisitions and makes bankruptcy, exemption, priority, and collection-authority checks prerequisites for consequential action.

sections.heading: 1. Build an evidence-first docket pipeline before automating decisions
paragraphs: Design the pipeline around a case event, not an AI conversation. The full-time operator owns intake, queue economics, and client communication; three contractors cover authorized research, bookkeeping, and licensed attorney work under separate engagements. Contractor status does not create permission to practice law or collect in a jurisdiction requiring a license. Each accepted file receives a case identifier, court identifier, creditor identity, debtor entity identifier, judgment date, entered amount, assignment evidence, and source-document digest. Use PACER for federal records and the relevant state court portal for state proceedings, through permitted access methods and approved accounts. A Python worker can ingest permitted downloads with urllib.request, normalize timestamps with datetime, and deduplicate documents with hashlib. Store transactional state in PostgreSQL through a separately reviewed deployment integration, or SQLite for a genuinely single-worker installation. Keep original files immutable and attach extracted claims to page references. Treat the 15 mapped plays as consumers of this shared evidence layer, not as permission to reuse assumptions across jurisdictions. A commercial guaranty, consumer obligation, HOA assessment, and purchased judgment can require different authority checks even when the same person appears in the docket.

Send only minimized, authorized document excerpts to an approved LLM endpoint, with retention settings consistent with the engagement. Ask for a fixed JSON schema containing extracted values, quoted source spans, page numbers, and explicit review reasons. Python validates field types, checks dates against the source, and rejects unsupported assertions; the model never supplies a deadline from memory. Treat docket text as untrusted input, including instructions embedded in exhibits. A rule registry stores jurisdiction, rule citation, effective dates, triggering event, calendar convention, and attorney reviewer. California Code of Civil Procedure section 683.020 supplies a general ten-year enforcement framework subject to exceptions and renewal rules, not a universal countdown for every obligation. Build proposed dates from reviewed rules, then require the responsible professional to confirm consequential deadlines against the operative docket. Bankruptcy alerts invoke a stay-review workflow under 11 U.S.C. section 362. Section 108(c) requires separate analysis; software must not assume every state limitation period simply stops running. Changes to a trigger date invalidate downstream calculations and generate a visible correction task. Every proposed filing remains a draft until the authorized person reviews the actual source packet.

Measure automation against a stable workload rather than counting colorful dashboard actions. For an illustrative monthly cohort of 1,000 routine research, qualification, fulfillment-preparation, and acquisition-administration work items, the manual baseline is ten minutes each, or 10,000 minutes. Suppose 750 items complete extraction and routing automatically but retain one minute of human verification each; 250 exceptions require eight minutes each. Human handling becomes 2,750 minutes, a 72.5% reduction, while straight-through machine processing covers 75% of items. That result does not mean 75% of enforcement decisions are automated. Consequential approvals within this routine cohort must fit the measured review time; contested litigation and complex priority opinions remain separately budgeted work. Track corrections, missed triggers, stale sources, and reopened exceptions alongside minutes saved. Sample completed low-risk extractions weekly and inspect every material deadline change. Require four consecutive measured weeks before treating the reduction as an operating assumption. If exception volume rises, narrow the supported courts or document types instead of suppressing review. The useful deliverable is a reproducible evidence packet with an accountable reviewer, not an impressive percentage detached from case consequences.

sections.heading: 2. Reconcile every payment and price every automated run
paragraphs: Build payment processing as an append-only ledger of observed events, not a spreadsheet that overwrites yesterday's balance. A signed bank or payment-provider webhook reaches a narrow receiver that verifies the signature over the raw request body, checks timestamp freshness, and records the provider event identifier before returning success. Python hmac and hashlib can implement provider-specified verification without inventing a signature format. Unique constraints prevent duplicate posting, while a durable queue separates receipt from reconciliation. Use decimal.Decimal for money and retain currency, value date, payer reference, case identifier, and source transaction identifier. Distinguish pending funds, settled funds, returned payments, creditor liabilities, earned service fees, and recoverable expenses. Allocate interest and principal only through a reviewed jurisdiction-specific ledger rule. A receipt is not automatically earned revenue, and an earned fee is not automatically available cash. Where funds belong in an attorney trust account or another required custodial arrangement, the recovery operator does not route them through an ordinary operating account. Bookkeeping prepares the allocation; the authorized signatory controls disbursement. Reversal events create linked compensating entries rather than deleting the original receipt, preserving the complete creditor statement history.

Reconcile the scorecard using recognized service fees exclusively. An illustrative 25% fee on settled client recoveries produces $60,000 of Conservative revenue from $240,000 collected, $280,000 of Base revenue from $1,120,000 collected, and $500,000 of Scaled revenue from $2,000,000 collected. These collection amounts are explanatory assumptions, not additional scorecard revenue or promised recoveries. Total annual operating costs must equal $48,000, $196,000, and $300,000 respectively, leaving exactly $12,000 at 20%, $84,000 at 30.0%, and $200,000 at 40%. Conservative and Base retain 1 FT + 3 C; Scaled uses 2 FT + 4 C. Contractor headcount does not imply four full-time salaries. The stated $2,000–$12,000 monthly operating range should be tracked as a planning range for recurring overhead, while the scenario reconciliation must also include variable contractor work, acquisition, research, and operator-borne enforcement expenses. The Base cost envelope averages about $16,333 monthly when all annual costs are included. Assign each expense to the correct bucket and prevent recoverable client advances from being mistaken for earned fees. A larger judgment face amount improves neither revenue nor margin until actual economics support recognition.

Price automation at the work-item level before buying a larger stack. Assume each routine run consumes $0.18 of parsing, $0.08 of LLM inference, $0.04 of orchestration, and $0.12 of storage and monitoring allocation: $0.42 total. At 1,000 monthly runs, that is $420 of machine cost. The earlier 2,750 human minutes equal 45.833 hours; at an illustrative loaded $45 hourly rate, review costs $2,062.50. Combined monthly handling cost is $2,482.50, or $2.4825 per run, compared with a $7,500 labor-only manual baseline. Annualized, the modeled handling bundle costs $29,790 and belongs inside the Base $196,000 cost envelope, not on top of it. These assumptions exclude separately priced court retrieval, specialist opinions, contested proceedings, acquisition spend, and disbursement work outside the routine cohort. Vendor quotes and measured time must replace assumptions before committing capacity. Retry transient failures with bounded exponential backoff, then move exhausted jobs to an exception queue. During a provider outage, accept no blind ledger updates: reconcile bank statements manually, preserve event identifiers, and replay only after duplicate detection passes. A cheap run that misallocates client money is an expensive operational defect.

sections.heading: 3. Turn reviewed knowledge into creditor acquisition loops
paragraphs: Build distribution for creditors and referral partners, not for public exposure of debtors. Programmatic pages should explain specific commercial recovery workflows: locating an entered judgment, preparing assignment records, assessing enforcement costs, or organizing a lien-priority review. Publish a page only when its jurisdictional differences justify distinct content and a named reviewer has checked the sources. An LLM can draft from the approved rule registry, but it cannot invent recoverability statistics, attorney relationships, or local office locations. Use Google Search Console to monitor search queries and a first-party intake form to capture creditor authorization, court, judgment date, and available documents. Do not collect a full sensitive case file through an unrestricted marketing form. A Python webhook validates the submission, creates a deduplicated lead, and sends a secure upload invitation after basic screening. Record source attribution without leaking debtor names into analytics URLs. Separate marketing contacts from case subjects so a debtor never enters a creditor prospecting sequence because their name appeared in a docket. If a page's governing authority changes, remove its automated recommendations until a reviewer refreshes the content and confirms any linked intake logic.

Make the referral loop useful before making it viral. Give commercial litigators, credit managers, and receivables teams a reusable judgment-transfer checklist, a sample evidence index, and a plain explanation of case acceptance criteria. The artifact should save partner labor even when no referral occurs. Allow partners to forward the public checklist while keeping client documents inside controlled workspaces. After a completed engagement, request permission to publish a genuinely de-identified process case study; removing a name alone may not prevent identification through a distinctive judgment amount or court history. Avoid referral payments that conflict with applicable attorney professional-conduct rules or collection restrictions. For outbound email, target verified business creditor roles using lawfully obtained contact data, truthful sender information, accurate subjects, a valid postal address, and an effective opt-out process under 15 U.S.C. section 7704. Maintain suppression across every sending system and honor statutory timing. Do not expand automatically into texts or autodialed calls, which require separate analysis under 47 U.S.C. section 227 and implementing rules. A referral engine fails when convenience turns case records into unauthorized marketing data or when an automated follow-up ignores a recipient's objection.

Model acquisition as cohorts with delayed cash, because the scorecard allows six to twenty-four months to the first deal. An illustrative annual cohort starts with 240 qualified creditor inquiries, converts 60 into accepted engagements, and eventually produces 20 paying matters averaging $14,000 of recognized fees. That yields the Base $280,000, but only in the period when those fees qualify for recognition; signing all 60 this year does not create this year's revenue. At the illustrative 25% fee, each paying matter corresponds to $56,000 of client collections, and twenty produce $1,120,000 of underlying recoveries. A $24,000 acquisition allocation implies $100 per qualified inquiry, $400 per accepted engagement, and $1,200 per paying matter. Include that allocation inside the $196,000 Base cost envelope alongside the $29,790 routine handling bundle, leaving $142,210 for all remaining modeled costs. Track intake qualification, acceptance, collectible-asset evidence, realized fees, and elapsed months separately. Stop scaling a channel that supplies large nominal judgments but repeated insolvency findings. When organic traffic falls, prioritize partner checklists and existing creditor renewals rather than publishing hundreds of unreviewed jurisdiction pages. Acquisition quality is measured by collectible, authorized work, not database size.

sections.heading: 4. Isolate statutory-interest experiments and scale through recoverable failures
paragraphs: Apply the same evidence architecture to hoa_super_lien_tax_deed_redemption_arbitrage, the TRACK_1 play for HOA Super-Lien & Sub-Threshold Tax-Deed Statutory Redemption Arbitrage, without turning it into a universal title strategy. A small purchase price changes capital exposure, not statutory notice requirements, lien priority, or redemption rights. Nevada Revised Statutes section 116.3116 supplies an HOA lien framework whose priority and enforceability require transaction-specific review of the applicable statutory version, related provisions, recorded instruments, payments, and foreclosure history. Do not assume acquiring an assessment claim conveys an unrestricted enforcement right or extinguishes a senior interest. Texas Tax Code section 34.21 supplies a different tax-sale redemption structure, including different periods for qualifying homestead, agricultural, mineral, and other property categories. Keep these jurisdictions and instruments in separate rule records. Python can assemble the title chronology, notice evidence, redemption dates, and cost ledger; an LLM can flag missing documents. Counsel must determine what interest can actually be acquired and enforced. Neither tool establishes valid title from a docket summary. Treat unresolved priority, deficient notice, or bankruptcy as reasons to suspend bidding, not as opportunities for a more optimistic automated valuation.

Use bounded arithmetic to expose the play's fragility. Suppose counsel confirms an assignable HOA interest with $2,600 of realistically available net proceeds before acquisition and operator costs. A $1,200 purchase, $300 diligence budget, and $500 operator-borne enforcement budget create $2,000 of modeled exposure and a $600 spread, or 30% on that exposure before additional overhead and timing effects. Another $600 of required enforcement work eliminates the spread entirely. This example does not assert that $2,600 receives statutory priority. For a separate Texas example, assume counsel confirms an $8,000 eligible redemption basis and a first-year redemption calculation carrying the applicable 25% premium. The resulting $2,000 premium is a conditional statutory calculation, not a 25% annual yield or assured recovery; $800 of unreimbursed costs would leave $1,200 before overhead and capital costs. If redemption never occurs, evaluate the actual remaining interest rather than projecting the premium forever. These investment illustrations sit outside the canonical service-fee scenarios. Suspend bidding when evidence fails, seek available statutory refunds where the facts and law permit them, and limit acquisitions to counsel-cleared interests. Never book the acquisition principal or a hypothetical premium as ordinary judgment recovery service revenue.

Scale the shared system only after its failure paths work. Maintain separate queues for routine extraction, uncertain identity, deadline review, bankruptcy, payment mismatch, acquisition review, and partner intake. Give each queue an accountable owner, a response target, and a safe paused state. A bankruptcy flag blocks affected collection actions but still permits internal preservation and review; a broken court connector creates a manual retrieval task rather than silently treating yesterday's docket as current. Test restoration from backups and rebuild case state from retained events before expanding volume. Use least-privilege service credentials, encrypted document storage, redacted application logs, and recorded access reviews. Retain source evidence according to the engagement and applicable requirements rather than keeping everything indefinitely. Within the $10,000–$75,000 startup range, reserve capital for long acquisition cycles and necessary specialist review before optional software. At Scaled, assign the second full-time person to operations quality and reconciliation, and use four contractors for bounded specialist capacity. Preserve the $500,000 fee revenue, $300,000 total cost, and $200,000 owner profit arithmetic. If backlogs exceed capacity, restrict intake or reprice documented scope; never make the margin work by removing source checks, stay review, or payment controls.

chapters.question_prompt: How do you structure a lean 1 FT + 3 C (4 people) -> 2 FT + 4 C (6 people) pod, enforce weekly scorecards, and build transferable books that command a premium exit multiple (or durable cash cow)?
chapters.title: Pod Architecture, Contractor KPIs & Exit Valuation
chapters.subtitle: Commercial Judgment Pods, Bankruptcy-Stay Controls, Lien-Priority Evidence, Cohort Ledgers & Transferable Recovery Books
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #8, Judgment Recovery, ranks #28 with a 79/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. Its 15 mapped plays become valuable only when a small pod converts lawful casework into documented, transferable service-fee earnings. Start with 1 FT + 3 C: an owner-operator, docket researcher, asset-and-priority analyst, and independently retained enforcement attorney. Expand to 2 FT + 4 C by adding an operations lead and reconciliation specialist. The canonical annual owner profits are $12,000 Conservative, $84,000 Base, and $200,000 Scaled. This chapter assigns seats, contractor deliverables, weekly evidence-based KPIs, 25% concentration ceilings, and cohort accounting. It also separates illustrative buyer multiples from supported earnings, showing how assignment rights, written IP transfers, and repeatable cash controls support either a sale or a durable owner-operated book.

sections.heading: 1. Assign Fifteen Recovery Plays to Four Seats Before Adding Two
paragraphs: Translate Candidate #8's 15 mapped operator plays into fifteen execution lanes for this chapter: creditor sourcing, judgment intake, docket screening, assignment verification, debtor identity resolution, lawful asset research, exemption screening, bankruptcy monitoring, lien-priority analysis, enforcement budgeting, attorney handoff, settlement administration, payment reconciliation, deadline renewal, and creditor reporting. These are working lane labels, not fifteen separate jobs. The baseline pod has one full-time owner and three contractors: a docket researcher, an asset-and-priority analyst, and independently retained enforcement counsel. Counsel remains responsible for legal judgments and representation within the engagement; the operator does not direct legal conclusions or sell unauthorized representation. Give every matter one owner, one stage, one next action, and one dated evidence packet. Airtable can hold workflow metadata, while a restricted document repository holds assignments, court orders, research provenance, and payment support. Keep sensitive identifiers out of general task descriptions. Separate a judgment's face amount from collectible assets and from the operator's fee entitlement. A large docket entry with a disputed assignment, exhausted collateral, or senior tax lien is a research exception, not productive inventory. Maintain a lane-to-seat register so no deadline depends on remembering which contractor last touched the file.

Buy contractor outputs rather than attendance. An illustrative research order pays $45 for an accepted docket packet containing the judgment, service history, last enforcement activity, and jurisdiction-specific renewal dates. An illustrative asset order pays $150 for a sourced identity-and-priority memorandum, with unresolved conflicts explicitly listed. These are purchasing assumptions to test locally, not market quotations or additions to the canonical profit cases. Require delivery within three business days after complete inputs, correction of attributable defects within two business days, and immediate escalation of a discovered bankruptcy or identity mismatch. Independently validate every proposed enforcement packet; sample routine research after acceptance and increase sampling when defects recur. Pay counsel under a separate engagement using locally permitted billing arrangements. Do not convert the research contractor into a percentage-paid legal intermediary or share attorney fees with a nonlawyer where prohibited. Contract labels alone do not establish independent status: review actual control, economic dependence, and applicable state tests with employment counsel. Track effective accepted-unit cost, including rework and supervision. Cheap packets become expensive when the owner spends an hour repairing identifiers or when a missed renewal destroys an otherwise collectible claim. Set purchase limits before issuing assignments, then reconcile accepted deliverables against invoices.

Scale to two full-time seats and four contractors by adding an operations lead and a reconciliation specialist, not another salesperson first. The owner retains creditor relationships, case economics, and exception decisions; the operations lead owns queues, service levels, evidence completeness, and contractor acceptance. The four contractors remain research, asset analysis, counsel, and reconciliation. Headcount describes seats, not four full-time contractor workloads. Counsel's capacity and conflicts must fit the chosen jurisdictions; narrow geographic intake rather than silently adding an unbudgeted legal bench. Use a six-week workload study before expansion: count accepted packets, owner exception hours, deadline backlog, payment exceptions, and realizable fees. Add the operations seat only when recurring contribution can fund its loaded cost through collection delays. The canonical startup capital range is $10,000–$75,000, and first-deal timing is 6–24 months, so apparent pipeline cannot substitute for liquidity. Treat the $2,000–$12,000 monthly operating-expense range as a planning input whose included categories must be reconciled with full scenario expenses. It cannot describe all scaled annual costs, which total $300,000. Cross-train the operations lead on creditor reporting and the owner on reconciliation review, while preserving independent approval of payment changes and disbursements.

callout.title: Protect Scarce Owner Hours Before Buying More Leads
callout.body: A small recovery pod wins through clean evidence and selective case economics, not through accumulating impressive judgment balances.
items: Require the analyst to show senior claims beside each asset; gross property value without priority analysis misstates the collection opportunity.
Attach the source docket entry and calculation basis to every renewal date; a calendar reminder without its legal starting point is fragile.
Use a paid sample packet before a contractor receives a portfolio, and include a known identity collision to test escalation discipline.
Record the owner's repair minutes against each rejected packet; renegotiate or replace vendors using total accepted-unit cost rather than headline pricing.

sections.heading: 2. Run a Weekly Evidence Scorecard That Cannot Reward Unsafe Volume
paragraphs: Run a forty-five-minute weekly operating review from one frozen reporting extract. The owner chairs the baseline review; the operations lead prepares it after scaling. Report opening active matters, accepted intake, closures, blocked matters, and closing active matters so inventory reconciles. Divide completed on-time tasks by tasks actually due that week; do not improve performance by moving due dates after they pass. Define first-pass acceptance as packets accepted without material correction divided by packets delivered. Start with a 95% operating target, then calibrate against observed complexity rather than declaring it an industry benchmark. Track bankruptcy-check freshness, court-deadline coverage, payment-match aging, and fee contribution by cohort alongside throughput. Every exception gets an owner, next action, and date. Report pending enforcement separately from research-ready files, because ten queued levies can consume more counsel capacity than fifty preliminary screens. No contractor receives a volume bonus for unverified assets, letters sent, or dollars of judgment principal. Reward accepted evidence and resolved exceptions within authorized scope. Keep the raw extract and meeting decisions in a dated folder so a buyer can reproduce performance instead of trusting a dashboard screenshot. Discuss repeated misses as a capacity or specification problem before assigning more work.

Make bankruptcy and identity controls independent of the weekly meeting. Under 11 U.S.C. section 362, a bankruptcy petition generally stays specified collection and enforcement activity; counsel determines application, exceptions, and any required relief. Screen at intake and immediately before an enforcement instruction or disbursement decision affected by bankruptcy. Record the searched identifiers, timestamp, source, and reviewer. A new filing moves the matter into a restricted status and alerts counsel; automation must not issue the next demand while someone investigates. PACER supplies federal docket access, but account availability does not eliminate identity matching or court-specific source checks. Commercial focus also does not justify assuming every file lies outside consumer-debt rules. Document the underlying transaction and evaluate the definitions in 15 U.S.C. section 1692a when a personal guaranty, mixed-purpose obligation, or consumer transaction appears. Access to consumer reports requires a valid permissible purpose under 15 U.S.C. section 1681b where that law applies. Vendor credentials are not permission to search any person. Route disputed authority, exemptions, service defects, and licensing questions to counsel before external action. Preserve the decision and supporting facts in the matter record, including why a seemingly attractive enforcement path was rejected.

Set a hard 25% ceiling for each creditor customer and each related debtor or payor group, measured separately across trailing-twelve-month recognized fees and probability-weighted expected fees on active matters. Group affiliates using documented common control; splitting one creditor into several account names does not create diversification. During startup, concentration may exceed the ceiling mechanically. Show the breach openly, pause additional discretionary exposure to that group, and assign a dated diversification plan rather than misstating compliance. Measure referral-source dependence separately, also capped at 25% of trailing recognized fees attributed to introductions. One law firm sending most cases can create commercial fragility even when underlying creditors differ. Use a second view of cash collections because one delayed large recovery can distort either measure. A base business with $280,000 annual recognized service fees therefore permits no group above $70,000 on the trailing-fee measure; the scaled ceiling is $125,000 against $500,000. Those are fee limits, not judgment-balance limits. Model the disappearance of the largest group and a ninety-day payment delay before adding fixed payroll. Keep concentration decisions connected to the fifteen execution lanes: sourcing changes the mix, intake controls acceptance, and reporting shows whether diversification actually reached earned fees.

callout.title: Verify Four Conditions Before Releasing Enforcement Work
callout.body: These checks apply to each matter, not merely to contractor onboarding. An unresolved result blocks the affected action while other authorized work continues.
items: Verify judgment identity, creditor authority, assignment chain, and counsel's representation scope against executed documents and the current docket.
Verify bankruptcy status using current searches, and obtain counsel's recorded direction on any stay, exception, relief, or uncertain debtor match.
Verify applicable licensing, debt classification, exemptions, data-access authority, and lien priority before selecting an enforcement method.
Verify the expenditure cap, estimated net collection waterfall, named reviewer, and approved payment instructions before releasing funds or instructions.

sop_steps.action: Export matter stages, task dates, accepted outputs, fee entries, and exceptions.
sop_steps.detail: Preserve the extract with its reporting cutoff and reconcile opening and closing matter counts.

sop_steps.title: Separate safety exceptions from productivity misses
sop_steps.action: Review bankruptcy, identity, deadline, and payment-control exceptions first.
sop_steps.detail: Restrict affected actions immediately; assign counsel or the responsible reviewer a documented next step.

sop_steps.action: Issue scoped work orders using backlog, defect rates, and approved purchase limits.

sop_steps.action: Reconcile earned fees, cohort costs, affiliate exposure, and owner exception hours.
sop_steps.detail: Record corrective decisions, accountable seats, and due dates in the same dated operating packet.

sections.heading: 3. Build Accrual and Cohort Books That Reconcile to the Canonical Cases
paragraphs: Maintain a matter subledger beneath the general ledger. Each matter needs creditor and debtor identifiers, engagement date, intake cohort, judgment principal, separately tracked interest, recovery receipts, client liabilities, fee terms, earned fees, direct costs, and remittance status. Judgment principal is operational reference data, not service revenue. For an illustrative collection, $100,000 received under a 30% earned service-fee agreement produces $30,000 operator revenue and $70,000 owed to the creditor before any separately authorized expense allocation. Do not post the entire receipt to sales and later call the remittance an expense. Use counsel or an appropriately authorized custodian for client funds where required; the operator's access and account structure must match applicable licensing and trust-account rules. The earned-fee trigger comes from the contract and the accounting policy reviewed by the accountant, including reversals, disputes, and amounts subject to refund. A signed recovery mandate or speculative asset estimate does not establish earned revenue. If a valid earned fee becomes receivable before cash arrives, record its basis and collectibility assessment. Reconcile bank activity, client liabilities, and fee entries monthly, with a different reviewer approving changes to creditor bank details. Never fund payroll with client balances awaiting remittance.

Use three reconciliations to keep the published scenarios intact: revenue to earned-fee entries, expenses to supported accruals, and profit to owner economics. Conservative revenue of $60,000 less $48,000 expenses produces $12,000 annual owner net profit at 20%. Base revenue of $280,000 less $196,000 expenses produces $84,000 at 30.0%. Scaled revenue of $500,000 less $300,000 expenses produces $200,000 at 40%. The first two cases use 1 FT + 3 C; Scaled uses 2 FT + 4 C. Do not change those totals to accommodate a preferred staffing narrative. An illustrative Base expense allocation is $72,000 contractor delivery, $44,000 unreimbursed enforcement and case costs, $24,000 systems and data, $20,000 acquisition, $18,000 insurance and professional support, and $18,000 other overhead. These six categories total $196,000; they are a budgeting allocation, not a second scorecard. Accrue accepted contractor work when incurred rather than shifting invoices into the next month to polish margins. Owner profit is not automatically buyer EBITDA or seller discretionary earnings. Document existing owner compensation and actual duties before making any replacement-cost adjustment, and avoid subtracting a salary already captured in expenses. Show every adjustment as a bridge, never as a silent rewrite.

Cohort reporting reveals whether the pod collects old wins while replenishing the book with weak cases. Group matters by intake quarter, creditor source, jurisdiction, and enforcement path. For each cohort, report accepted matters, cash recovered for clients, recognized service fees, direct expense, allocated delivery cost, elapsed months, and unresolved exposure. Compare cohorts at matching ages; a three-month cohort cannot fairly compete with a two-year cohort on lifetime collections. Track realized contribution separately from probability-weighted future fees and identify the assumption owner for each forecast. Insolvent debtors, bankruptcy stays, and enforcement costs are Candidate #8's central risks, so record write-down reasons rather than burying failures in a broad overhead account. A renewal deadline may preserve a claim without creating current fee revenue. A lien may improve position without producing spendable cash. QuickBooks Online can maintain the ledger, while a controlled spreadsheet or database carries matter-level waterfalls and cohort schedules. Lock closed periods, log adjustments, and reconcile exports before sharing them. Reserve cash against approved future case spending and fixed commitments, not against gross judgment balances. The owner's monthly decision is whether another dollar of authorized casework improves expected retained fees enough to justify delay and loss exposure.

sections.heading: 4. Price Transferable Earnings, Not Judgment Face Value
paragraphs: A buyer acquires enforceable relationships, reliable earnings, and an operating system; a folder of judgments alone does not establish enterprise value. Separate the company's sale from any transfer of creditor engagements, judgment assignments, servicing rights, or attorney relationships. Review anti-assignment provisions, change-of-control terms, creditor consent requirements, applicable licenses, and court-record requirements individually. Counsel evaluates whether substitution or additional filings are needed, including under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 69 where federal enforcement is involved. State procedure remains central: California Code of Civil Procedure section 683.020 generally addresses the ten-year enforcement period, subject to renewal and other applicable provisions. Do not turn that example into a nationwide deadline. Inventory contractor-created templates, scripts, research schemas, training materials, and reporting formats. Under 17 U.S.C. section 204(a), a transfer of copyright ownership generally requires a signed writing; paying an invoice alone is insufficient. Obtain express assignments of applicable rights, while identifying preexisting tools, licensed materials, and excluded third-party data. Vendor subscriptions and restricted research outputs may be nontransferable. Maintain a rights register that links each operational asset to its owner, permitted use, transfer terms, and supporting document. A buyer cannot inherit permissions the seller never possessed.

Use valuation multiples as explicit negotiation sensitivities, not asserted market evidence. For an illustrative owner-operated asset sale, test 2.0–3.0 times verified seller discretionary earnings only after an accountant reconciles that measure to the books. If, purely for sensitivity, normalized earnings equal the canonical owner profits, Conservative indicates $24,000–$36,000, Base $168,000–$252,000, and Scaled $400,000–$600,000. These are enterprise-value illustrations before debt, excess cash, working capital adjustments, taxes, and transaction costs. They are not quoted offers. For a manager-run buyer, first subtract any genuinely incremental replacement expense. If Scaled profit requires $80,000 of additional loaded management cost beyond existing expenses, adjusted earnings become $120,000; an illustrative 3.0–4.0 times sensitivity gives $360,000–$480,000. That comparison shows why a higher multiple can produce a lower price when the earnings basis changes. Use actual replacement duties and compensation quotes, not a convenient round add-back. Earnings volatility, single-case windfalls, weak assignment rights, unresolved licensing, and concentrated creditors can drive value below these ranges or make a sale impractical. Evidence of repeatable cohorts, independent management, and clean transfers supports negotiating toward the upper end; it does not mechanically earn a premium. Validate pricing against current comparable transactions before marketing.

Build the sale file quarterly even when the preferred outcome is continued ownership. Include monthly reconciled statements, fee-recognition policy, cohort schedules, concentration reports, contractor agreements, IP assignments, license records, court-deadline controls, and a schedule of disputed matters. Begin buyer diligence with aggregated and redacted information; release identifiable debtor or creditor records only under appropriate authority, confidentiality terms, and access restrictions. Log access and revoke it when discussions end. A cash-cow decision uses the same evidence: measure owner hours, maintenance spending, replacement case supply, collection delays, and downside liquidity. Do not compare a headline purchase price with annual owner profit while ignoring taxes, seller notes, contingent payments, and the labor needed to keep earning. If part of consideration depends on future collections, define qualifying cohorts, the retained service-fee basis, permitted deductions, reporting rights, collection conduct, and dispute procedures. Avoid an earnout based on gross debtor payments that rewards revenue inflation or uneconomic enforcement. Complete a controlled owner-absence rehearsal covering at least one reporting and reconciliation cycle. Record every intervention, fix the underlying dependency, and repeat. The strongest exit preparation is proving that all fifteen lanes continue functioning when the owner's inbox is no longer the system of record.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #8, Judgment Recovery, ranks #28 with a 79/100 Money-to-Manpower Score across 15 mapped plays. Launch the operating system in thirty days, not a promise of immediate collections: the canonical time to first deal is six to twenty-four months. This sprint assigns docket screening, lawful authority, asset verification, lien analysis, and payment reconciliation to one full-time operator plus three contractors. A $6,000 first-month spending ceiling and evidence-based Day 30/60/90 decisions prevent speculative enforcement from consuming working capital. The annual owner-profit cases remain $12,000 Conservative, $84,000 Base, and $200,000 Scaled. Those outcomes derive from recognized service fees, never judgment face amounts or client assets. Expand only after authority, priority-adjusted recovery prospects, contractor capacity, and runway withstand review.

sections.heading: 1. Days 1–7: Build the Authority, Evidence, and Spending System
paragraphs: Start with one state, one commercial judgment segment, and one documented enforcement route. The first deliverable is an operating boundary, not a debtor contact list. Record the originating obligation, judgment court, creditor identity, debtor entity, judgment date, balance method, and counsel responsible for interpreting local procedure. Commercial classification follows the transaction's purpose, not merely the presence of a business name; 15 U.S.C. § 1692a(5) defines covered consumer debt, while state collection rules may reach further. Have local counsel determine licensing, registration, bonding, assignment formalities, and which activities require an attorney before outreach or representation begins. An assignment does not itself authorize a nonlawyer to practice law. Separate creditor acquisition from debtor communications so marketing staff cannot drift into collection activity. Use PACER for federal records and the relevant state court portal for state judgments; retain source identifiers and retrieval dates rather than treating an aggregator summary as controlling evidence. Set up an encrypted case repository, role-based permissions, and a deadline ledger with a human reviewer. By Day 7, every proposed activity must have an owner, a permitted method, a spending limit, and a stop condition. Unresolved authority questions block the affected activity, not unrelated research.

Use the following chapter-level execution map to operationalize Candidate #8's fifteen mapped plays; these labels organize the sprint rather than assert an external taxonomy. P01 is segment selection; P02 is creditor sourcing; P03 is docket verification; P04 is judgment validity and deadline review; P05 is assignment or engagement authority; P06 is bankruptcy and discharge screening; P07 is lawful asset research; P08 is lien and exemption analysis; P09 is recovery underwriting; P10 is attorney-directed discovery; P11 is attorney-directed enforcement; P12 is authorized settlement coordination; P13 is payment reconciliation; P14 is creditor reporting; and P15 is portfolio triage and renewal tracking. One full-time lead owns sourcing, underwriting, client communication, and contractor coordination. Contractor A is local enforcement counsel; contractor B performs permitted records research; contractor C maintains bookkeeping and deadline controls. Counsel retains professional judgment and required client relationships. Initial weekly capacity is forty lead hours, four counsel hours, eight research hours, and three bookkeeping hours, purchased within written caps. This is a four-person pod, not four full-time salaries. Each case card identifies its current play, next evidence request, responsible person, and maximum authorized spend. An overdue task moves into the daily exception queue instead of silently aging.

Authorize no more than $6,000 of committed launch spending through Day 30: $1,800 for counsel and authority review, $900 for research support, $450 for bookkeeping setup, $350 for court records and permitted data, $250 for software, $650 for operating administration and insurance-related setup, $600 for approved case disbursements, and $1,000 contingency. Count purchase commitments when approved, not when invoices arrive, and do not count client money as available working capital. These allocations are planning limits, not vendor quotes; replace estimates with written prices before ordering. If mandatory licensing or insurance consumes the allowance, reduce activity or fund the difference before proceeding. The canonical startup range is $10,000–$75,000 and monthly operating expense range is $2,000–$12,000; neither authorizes spending beyond available cash. Preserve at least six months of measured recurring overhead outside the sprint budget. At a $2,000 monthly floor, completing the full $14,000 ninety-day plan therefore requires $26,000 of available capital before additional reserves. A $10,000 entrant should remain in lower-cost research and setup until funded for the chosen workload. Because first deals can take six to twenty-four months, six months of reserve is a minimum review threshold, not complete funding for every possible collection cycle.
